bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【漢紀三十四】起上章攝提格，盡旃蒙協洽，凡六年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 34】 From Shangzhang Shetige through Zhanmeng Xieqia—in all, six years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 34】 From the first year of the Shangzhang cycle through the last year of the Zhanmeng cycle—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖光武皇帝中之上

translations.literal: Founding Emperor Guangwu, Middle Part, Upper Section.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor Guangwu — Middle Part, Upper Section.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，丙辰，以舂陵鄉為章陵縣，世世復傜役，比豐、沛。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on the day bingchen, Chunling township was made Zhangling county; corvée and levies were remitted for all generations, on a par with Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, in the first month, on the day bingchen, Chunling township was made Zhangling county, with corvée and levies remitted for all generations, as at Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 2吳漢等拔朐，斬董憲、龐萌，江、淮、山東悉平。

translations.literal: 2. Wu Han and others took Ju, beheaded Dong Xian and Pang Meng; the Yangtze, Huai, and Shandong were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Wu Han and others captured Ju and beheaded Dong Xian and Pang Meng; the lands along the Yangtze, the Huai, and Shandong were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 諸將還京師，置酒賞賜。

translations.literal: The generals returned to the capital; wine was set out and rewards given.
translations.idiomatic: The generals returned to the capital, where the emperor feasted them and gave rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝積苦兵間，以隗囂遣子內侍，公孫述遠據邊垂，乃謂諸將曰：「且當置此兩子於度外耳。

translations.literal: The emperor, long wearied amid warfare, because Wei Xiao had sent his son in as attendant and Gongsun Shu held the far borderlands, thereupon said to the generals: "For now we ought to set these two fellows outside our reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, worn down by years of war, noted that Wei Xiao had sent his son as a hostage and that Gongsun Shu held the distant marches. He told his generals, "For now let us set these two aside."

sentences.zh: 」因休諸將於雒陽，分軍士於河內，數騰書隴、蜀，告示禍福。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he rested the generals at Luoyang, distributed troops to Henei, and repeatedly sent letters flying to Long and Shu, proclaiming fortune and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave his generals rest at Luoyang, posted troops in Henei, and again and again sent letters to Long and Shu proclaiming blessing and doom.

sentences.zh: 公孫述屢移書中國，自陳符命，冀以惑眾。

translations.literal: Gongsun Shu repeatedly sent letters to the central lands, himself presenting his mandate from omens, hoping thereby to delude the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu sent letter after letter to the central court, citing omens of his destined rule, hoping to sway men's minds.

sentences.zh: 帝與述書曰：「圖讖言公孫，即宣帝也。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote to Shu: "The charts and prophecies speak of 'Gongsun'—that means Emperor Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to Gongsun Shu: "The prophecies speak of 'Gongsun'—they mean Emperor Xuan."

sentences.zh: 代漢者姓當塗，其名高；

translations.literal: "He who replaces Han bears the surname Dangtu; his given name is Gao;"
translations.idiomatic: "'He who replaces Han bears the surname Dangtu; his given name is Gao;'—"

sentences.zh: 君豈高之身邪！

translations.literal: "are you perhaps Gao in person!"
translations.idiomatic: "are you that Gao in person?"

sentences.zh: 乃復以掌文為瑞，王莽何足效乎！

translations.literal: "Yet you again take palm-script as an auspice—how is Wang Mang worth imitating!"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet you again take palm-writing as a portent—Wang Mang is hardly worth imitating!"

sentences.zh: 君非吾賊臣亂子，倉卒時人皆欲為君事耳。

translations.literal: "You are not my rebel minister or disorderly son; in the rush of the moment everyone wished to serve you."
translations.idiomatic: "You are no rebel of mine; in the chaos everyone wished to serve you for a time."

sentences.zh: 君日月已逝，妻子弱小，當早為定計。

translations.literal: "Your sun and moon have already set; wife and children are young and weak—you ought early to settle your plan."
translations.idiomatic: "Your day is passing; your wife and children are young and weak. Settle your course soon."

sentences.zh: 天下神器，不可力爭，宜留三思！

translations.literal: "The sacred vessel of the realm cannot be seized by force—leave room for three thoughts!"
translations.idiomatic: "The Mandate is not won by force alone—think thrice before you act!"

sentences.zh: 」署曰「公孫皇帝」。

translations.literal: " The superscription read "Emperor Gongsun."
translations.idiomatic: " He addressed it to "Emperor Gongsun."

sentences.zh: 述不答。

translations.literal: Shu did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu did not answer.

sentences.zh: 其騎都尉平陵荊邯說述曰：「漢高祖起於行陳之中，兵破身困者數矣；

translations.literal: His Cavalry Commandant Jing Han of Pingling urged Shu: "Han Gaozu rose from the ranks of the marching camp; his army was broken and his person distressed many times;"
translations.idiomatic: His Cavalry Commandant Jing Han of Pingling urged Gongsun Shu: "Han Gaozu rose from the ranks; his armies were shattered and he himself brought low again and again;"

sentences.zh: 然軍敗復合，瘡愈復戰。

translations.literal: "yet when the army was defeated it gathered again; when wounds healed he fought again."
translations.idiomatic: "yet when his army broke it re-formed; when his wounds healed he fought again."

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 前死而成功，愈於卻就於滅亡也！

translations.literal: "To die forward yet succeed is better than to retreat toward destruction!"
translations.idiomatic: "To press on even unto death and win is better than to fall back toward ruin!"

sentences.zh: 隗囂遭遇運會，割有雍州，兵強士附，威加山東；

translations.literal: "Wei Xiao met with the turning of fortune, carved out Yong Province, had strong soldiers and attached warriors, and his prestige reached beyond the mountains east;
translations.idiomatic: "Wei Xiao seized his moment, held Yong Province, commanded strong armies and loyal men, and his fame reached east of the passes;"

sentences.zh: 遇更始政亂，復失天下，眾庶引領，四方瓦解，囂不及此時推危乘勝以爭天命，而退欲為西伯之事，尊師章句，賓友處士，偃武息戈，卑辭事漢，喟然自以文王復出也！

translations.literal: "when Gengshi's government fell into disorder he again lost the realm; the common folk craned their necks and the four quarters crumbled—yet Xiao did not at this time press the peril and ride victory to contend for Heaven's mandate, but withdrew wishing to play the Western Earl: honoring teachers and classical lines, keeping guest-friends and recluses, laying down arms and resting spears, with humble words serving Han, sighing to himself that King Wen had come again!"
translations.idiomatic: "when the Gengshi court collapsed he might have taken the realm—the people looked to him and the empire fell apart—yet he did not press his advantage and contend for the Mandate. Instead he played King Wen: honoring teachers and classical glosses, gathering scholars and recluses, laying down arms, humbling himself before Han, sighing that King Wen had returned!"

sentences.zh: 令漢帝釋關、隴之憂，專精東伐，四分天下而有其三；

translations.literal: "This let the Han emperor release his cares for the passes and Long, concentrate on eastern campaigns, and hold three parts of a realm quartered;
translations.idiomatic: "So the Han emperor left the passes and Long untroubled, turned east, and held three quarters of the realm;"

sentences.zh: 發間使，召攜貳，使西州豪傑咸居心於山東，則五分而有其四；

translations.literal: "send secret envoys, summon the hesitant and divided, and make the great men of the western provinces all set their hearts on the east—then of five parts he would hold four;
translations.idiomatic: "send secret agents, win over the wavering, and turn the western chieftains' hearts toward the east—then four parts in five would be his;"

sentences.zh: 若舉兵天水，必至沮潰，天水既定，則九分而有其八。

translations.literal: "if he raised troops at Tianshui they would surely break and flee; once Tianshui was settled, then of nine parts he would hold eight."
translations.idiomatic: "if he marched on Tianshui the enemy would break; with Tianshui secure, eight parts in nine would be his."

sentences.zh: 陛下以梁州之地，內奉萬乘，外給三軍，百姓愁困，不堪上命，將有王氏自潰之變矣！

translations.literal: "Your Majesty, with Liang Province's lands, within supplying the imperial carriage and without provisioning the Three Armies—the common people are bitter and distressed, unable to bear commands from above; there will be a Wang Mang-style collapse from within!"
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty holds Liang Province, supplying the throne within and the armies without, while the people groan under your demands—they cannot bear it. You will face a Wang Mang-style collapse from within!"

sentences.zh: 臣之愚計，以為宜及天下之望未絕，豪桀尚可招誘，急以此時發國內精兵，令田戎據江陵，臨江南之會，倚巫山之固，築壘堅守，傳檄吳、楚，長沙以南必隨風而靡。

translations.literal: "This servant's foolish plan holds that you ought, while the realm's hopes are not yet spent and bold men can still be enticed, urgently at this time send out the realm's elite troops, order Tian Rong to hold Jiangling, face the junction of the south of the Yangtze, lean on Wushan's strength, build ramparts and hold firm, send proclamations to Wu and Chu—the lands south of Changsha will surely bend like grass in the wind."
translations.idiomatic: "My counsel: while hope in you still lives and heroes may yet be won, strike now with your best troops. Put Tian Rong at Jiangling above the Yangtze junction, behind Wushan's ramparts, and hold fast. Send proclamations to Wu and Chu—the lands south of Changsha will bow like reeds in wind."

sentences.zh: 令延岑出漢中，定三輔，天水、隴西拱手自服。

translations.literal: "Order Yan Cen out from Hanzhong to settle the Three Metropolises; Tianshui and Longxi will fold their hands and submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Send Yan Cen from Hanzhong to secure the Three Metropolises; Tianshui and Longxi will surrender without a fight."

sentences.zh: 如此，海內震搖，冀有大利。

translations.literal: "Thus the realm within the seas would shake; we might hope for great gain."
translations.idiomatic: "Then the empire would tremble—and great profit might follow."

sentences.zh: 」述以問群臣，博士吳柱曰：「武王伐殷，八百諸侯不期同辭，然猶還師以待天命。

translations.literal: " Shu put the question to his ministers; the Erudite Wu Zhu said: "King Wu attacked Yin: eight hundred lords came together unbidden in one voice, yet he still turned the army back to await Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Shu asked his ministers. Erudite Wu Zhu said, "When King Wu attacked Yin, eight hundred lords came of one accord—yet he still withdrew his army to await Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 未聞無左右之助。

translations.literal: "One has not heard of lacking help at one's side"
translations.idiomatic: "No one has marched far without allies at hand"

sentences.zh: 而欲出師千里之外者也。

translations.literal: "yet wishing to send the army out a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: "yet wishing to march a thousand li beyond your borders."

sentences.zh: 」邯曰：「今東帝無尺十之柄，驅烏合之眾，跨馬陷敵，所向輒平，不亟乘時與之分功，而坐談武王之說，是復效隗囂欲為西伯也。

translations.literal: " Han said: "Now the eastern emperor lacks even a foot of ten in authority; he drives a flock of crows gathered, spurs his horse and breaks the enemy—where he turns all is soon level. If we do not urgently seize the time and share in his merit, but sit and discourse on King Wu's example, this is again to imitate Wei Xiao wishing to be the Western Earl."
translations.idiomatic: " Jing Han said, "The eastern emperor holds barely a finger's breadth of power. He drives a rabble, spurs his horse into the fray, and wins wherever he turns. If we do not seize this moment and share his conquests, but sit citing King Wu, we repeat Wei Xiao playing King Wen."

sentences.zh: 述然邯言，欲悉發北軍屯士及山東客兵，使延岑、田戎分出兩道，與漢中諸將合兵並勢。

translations.literal: Shu approved Han's words and wished to send out all northern-army garrison troops and eastern guest-soldiers, ordering Yan Cen and Tian Rong to divide into two routes and join the Hanzhong generals in combined force.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu agreed with Jing Han and planned to mobilize every northern garrison soldier and eastern mercenary, sending Yan Cen and Tian Rong by two routes to join the Hanzhong commanders in one thrust.

sentences.zh: 蜀人及其弟光以為不宜空國千里之外，決成敗於一舉，固爭之，述乃止。

translations.literal: Shu people and his younger brother Guang held that one ought not to empty the state a thousand li away and decide success or failure in a single throw; they firmly contested it, and Shu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu and his brother Guang argued that he must not strip the realm and stake everything on one throw a thousand li away. They pressed him hard, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 延岑、田戎亦數請兵立功，述終疑不聽，唯公孫氏得任事。

translations.literal: Yan Cen and Tian Rong also repeatedly begged troops to win merit; Shu to the end was suspicious and would not listen—only the house of Gongsun received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Cen and Tian Rong also begged again and again for troops to earn glory, but Gongsun Shu remained suspicious and refused. Only his own clan held office.

sentences.zh: 述廢銅錢，置鐵錢，貨幣不行，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Shu abolished copper cash and instituted iron money; currency did not circulate and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu abolished copper coin and issued iron money. Trade stalled and the people groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 為政苛細，察於小事，如為清水令時而已。

translations.literal: In government he was harsh and minute, scrutinizing small matters—just as when he had been magistrate of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was petty and exacting, obsessed with trifles—as when he had been magistrate of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 好改易郡縣官名。

translations.literal: He loved to change the official names of commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to rename commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 少嘗為郎，習漢家故事，出入法駕，鸞旗旄騎。

translations.literal: In youth he had once been a gentleman-attendant, versed in Han household precedents; going out and in he used the statutory imperial equipage—phoenix banners and pennoned horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had served as a court gentleman and knew Han ritual. He went abroad with imperial pomp—phoenix banners and pennoned escorts.

sentences.zh: 又立其兩子為王，食犍為、廣漢各數縣。

translations.literal: He also established his two sons as kings, with fiefs of several counties each in Qianwei and Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He also made his two sons kings, enfeoffing them with several counties each in Qianwei and Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「成敗未可知，戎士暴露而先王愛子，示無大志也！

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "Success or failure is not yet known; war-fighters are exposed to the elements while beloved sons are made kings first—this shows no great ambition!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him: "Victory is not yet certain. Your soldiers freeze in the field while you crown your sons—this shows small ambition!"

sentences.zh: 」述不從，由此大臣皆怨。

translations.literal: " Shu would not follow; from this the great ministers all resented.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not listen, and from that his ministers turned against him.

sentences.zh: 3馮異自長安入朝，帝謂公卿曰：「是我起兵時主簿也，為吾披荊棘，定關中。

translations.literal: 3. Feng Yi came from Chang'an to audience; the emperor said to the excellencies and ministers: "This was my registrar when I first raised troops; for me he cut through brambles and settled Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: 3. Feng Yi came from Chang'an to court. The emperor told the ministers, "This was my registrar when I first raised arms. He cut through the thorns for me and secured Guanzhong."

sentences.zh: 」既罷，賜珍寶、錢帛，詔曰：「倉卒蕪蔞亭豆粥，虖沱河麥飯，厚意久不報。

translations.literal: " When dismissed, he was granted treasures, cash, and silks; an edict said: "In haste at Wulou Pavilion, bean porridge; at Hutuo River, wheat meal—your deep kindness long unrewarded."
translations.idiomatic: " When the audience ended he gave him treasures, cash, and silk, with an edict: "Bean porridge at Wulou Pavilion, wheat gruel at Hutuo River—your kindness went long unrewarded."

sentences.zh: 」異稽首謝曰：「臣聞管仲謂桓公曰：『願君無忘射鉤，臣無忘檻車。

translations.literal: " Yi knocked his head and thanked him, saying: "Your servant has heard that Guan Zhong told Duke Huan: 'May my lord not forget the arrow that hooked him; may your servant not forget the caged cart."
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Yi kowtowed and said, "I have heard that Guan Zhong told Duke Huan of Qi: 'May my lord not forget the arrow that hooked you; may I not forget the prison cart.'"

sentences.zh: 』齊國賴之。

translations.literal: "' Qi relied on this."
translations.idiomatic: "' On that Qi stood."

sentences.zh: 臣今亦願國家無忘河北之難，小臣不敢忘巾車之恩。

translations.literal: "Your servant now also wishes the state not to forget the hardships north of the river; this petty servant dares not forget the kindness of the covered cart."
translations.idiomatic: "I too pray the realm will not forget the trials north of the river; I dare not forget the kindness of the covered cart."

sentences.zh: 」留十餘日，令與妻子還西。

translations.literal: " He was kept more than ten days, then ordered with wife and children to return west.
translations.idiomatic: " He stayed more than ten days, then was sent west with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 4申屠剛、杜林自隗囂所來，帝皆拜侍御史。

translations.literal: 4. Shentu Gang and Du Lin came from Wei Xiao's domain; the emperor invested both as Attendant Censors.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Shentu Gang and Du Lin came from Wei Xiao's camp; the emperor made both Attendant Censors.

sentences.zh: 以鄭興為太中大夫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xing was made Grand Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xing was appointed Grand Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 5三月，公孫述使田戎出江關，招其故眾，欲以取荊州，不克。

translations.literal: 5. In the third month, Gongsun Shu sent Tian Rong out through the Yangtze passes to summon his former followers, intending thereby to take Jing Province; he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: 5. In the third month Gongsun Shu sent Tian Rong through the river passes to rally his old followers and seize Jing Province. He failed.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔隗囂，欲從天水伐蜀。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict to Wei Xiao, wishing to march on Shu from Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Wei Xiao to join an invasion of Shu from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 囂上言：「白水險阻，棧閣敗絕。

translations.literal: Xiao memorialized upward: "Bai River is perilous and blocked; plank roads and passes are ruined and cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao replied: "The Bai River country is rugged; the plank roads are broken and impassable."

sentences.zh: 述性嚴酷，上下相患，須其罪惡孰著而攻之，此大呼響應之勢也。

translations.literal: "Shu's nature is harsh and cruel; above and below mistrust one another—we must wait until his crimes are fully manifest and then attack; this is the momentum of a great shout answered in echo."
translations.idiomatic: "Gongsun Shu is harsh and cruel; his court and people fear one another. Wait until his crimes are plain, then strike—the realm will answer like an echo to a shout."

sentences.zh: 」帝知其終不為用，乃謀討之。

translations.literal: " The emperor knew he would in the end not be employed and thereupon plotted to strike him down.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor knew Wei Xiao would never serve him and began planning his destruction.

sentences.zh: 6夏，四月，丙子，上行幸長安，謁園陵；

translations.literal: 6. In summer, the fourth month, on the day bingzi, the emperor traveled in person to Chang'an and visited the park tombs;
translations.idiomatic: 6. In summer, in the fourth month, on the day bingzi, the emperor went in person to Chang'an and visited the imperial tombs;

sentences.zh: 遣耿弇、蓋延等七將軍從隴道伐蜀，先使中郎將來歙奉璽書賜囂諭旨。

translations.literal: he sent the seven generals Geng Yan, Gai Yan, and others by the Long road to attack Shu, first dispatching the Palace Gentleman Lai Xi to bear the imperial-seal letter granting Xiao the edict's purport.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Geng Yan, Gai Yan, and five other generals against Shu by the Long road, and first dispatched Palace Gentleman Lai Xi with an imperial letter to instruct Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 囂復多設疑故，事久冘豫不決。

translations.literal: Xiao again set up many doubts and pretexts; the matter dragged on long, dilatory and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao raised objection after objection; days passed and he still would not decide.

sentences.zh: 歙遂發憤質素囂曰：「國家以君知臧否，曉廢興，故以手書暢意。

translations.literal: Xi thereupon flared in anger and confronted Xiao plainly: "The state, because you know good from ill and understand decline and rise, therefore sent a personal letter to express its intent fully."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Xi then burst out and confronted Wei Xiao: "The throne believes you know good from evil and rise from fall—that is why it sent you this personal letter."

sentences.zh: 足下推忠誠，既遣伯春委質，而反欲用佞惑之言，為族滅之計邪！

translations.literal: "You, sir, have professed loyalty and already sent Bochun as hostage—yet you turn back wishing to use flatterers' deluding words and make a plan for extermination of your clan!"
translations.idiomatic: "You pledged loyalty and sent your son Bochun as hostage—will you now heed flatterers and plot your clan's destruction?"

sentences.zh: 」因欲前刺囂。

translations.literal: " He thereupon wished to step forward and stab Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " He started forward to stab Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 囂起入，部勒兵將殺歙，歙徐杖節就車而去，囂使牛邯將兵圍守之。

translations.literal: Xiao rose and went inside, mustered troops intending to kill Xi; Xi slowly, staff and credentials in hand, went to his carriage and left; Xiao sent Niu Han to lead troops to surround and hold him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao rose and withdrew, called up troops to kill him. Lai Xi walked slowly, staff and credentials in hand, to his carriage and departed. Wei Xiao sent Niu Han to surround and detain him.

sentences.zh: 囂將王遵諫曰：「君叔雖單車遠使，而陛下之外兄也，殺之無損於漢，而隨以族滅。

translations.literal: Xiao's general Wang Zun remonstrated: "Junshu, though he came on a lone carriage as envoy far away, is nonetheless Your Majesty's maternal cousin; to kill him would not harm Han, but destruction of the clan would follow at once."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao's general Wang Zun urged: "Lai Xi came alone on a distant mission, but he is the emperor's cousin by marriage. Killing him would not hurt Han—but your clan would perish for it."

sentences.zh: 昔宋執楚使，遂有析骸易子之禍。

translations.literal: "In former times Song seized Chu's envoy, and thereupon came the calamity of splitting bones and exchanging children."
translations.idiomatic: "When Song seized Chu's envoy, fathers and sons starved until they bartered flesh."

sentences.zh: 小國猶不可辱，況於萬乘之主，重以伯春之命哉！

translations.literal: "A small state still may not be insulted—how much less a lord of ten thousand chariots, with Bochun's charge added!"
translations.idiomatic: "Even a small state must not be shamed—how much less an emperor, and with your son Bochun's life at stake!"

sentences.zh: 」歙為人有信義，言行不違，及往來遊說，皆可按覆；

translations.literal: " Xi as a man had trust and righteousness; words and deeds did not diverge; in coming and going to persuade, all could be checked and verified;
translations.idiomatic: " Lai Xi was a man of trust; his words matched his deeds, and every embassy he had made could be verified;

sentences.zh: 西州士大夫皆信重之，多為其言，故得免而東歸。

translations.literal: the gentlemen and grandees of the western provinces all trusted and honored him; many spoke for him—therefore he was spared and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: the western gentry all trusted him, and many spoke for him, so he was spared and sent east.

sentences.zh: 五月，己未，車駕至自長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day jiwei, the imperial carriage returned from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jiwei, the emperor returned from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隗囂遂發兵反，使王元據隴坻，伐木塞道。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao thereupon raised troops in rebellion, sent Wang Yuan to hold Longzhi, felled trees and blocked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao then rebelled, posted Wang Yuan at Longzhi, felled trees and blocked the roads.

sentences.zh: 諸將因與囂戰，大敗，各引兵下隴；

translations.literal: The generals thereupon fought Xiao and were utterly defeated; each led his troops down from Long;
translations.idiomatic: The generals fought him and were routed; each led his army down from the Long plateau;

sentences.zh: 囂追之急，馬武選精騎為後拒，殺數千人，諸軍乃得還。

translations.literal: Xiao pressed the pursuit hotly; Ma Wu selected elite horsemen as rear guard, killed several thousand, and the armies thereupon were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao pressed hard. Ma Wu chose elite cavalry as rearguard, slew several thousand, and the armies escaped.

sentences.zh: 7六月辛卯，詔曰：「夫張官置吏，所以為民也。

translations.literal: 7. On the day xinmao in the sixth month, an edict said: "To spread offices and set clerks is for the sake of the people."
translations.idiomatic: 7. On xinmao day in the sixth month an edict ran: "Offices exist for the people's sake."

sentences.zh: 今百姓遭難，戶口耗少，而縣官吏職，所置尚繁。

translations.literal: "Now the people suffer calamity; households and population are depleted and few, yet county official posts set remain still numerous."
translations.idiomatic: "The people have suffered war; households are few, yet county posts remain too many."

sentences.zh: 其令司隸、州牧各實所部，省減吏員，縣國不足置長吏者並之。

translations.literal: "Let the Director of the Capital and the provincial governors each verify their jurisdictions, reduce and cut official posts, and merge counties and kingdoms that cannot support chief clerks."
translations.idiomatic: "Let the Director of the Capital and the provincial governors audit their domains, cut posts, and merge counties too small to need their own magistrates."

sentences.zh: 」於是並省四百餘縣，吏職減損，十置其一。

translations.literal: " Thereupon more than four hundred counties were merged and cut; official posts were reduced—one set where ten had stood.
translations.idiomatic: " More than four hundred counties were merged; posts were cut to one in ten.

sentences.zh: 8〔秋〕，九月<ref>〔秋〕九月據《通鑑》通例補「秋」字。

translations.literal: 8. 〔Autumn〕, the ninth month<ref>〔Autumn〕—the character "autumn" for the ninth month is supplied per the Comprehensive Mirror's usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: 8. 〔Autumn〕, the ninth month<ref>〔Autumn〕—"autumn" is supplied for the ninth month per the Comprehensive Mirror's usual practice.

sentences.zh: </ref>，丙寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: </ref> On the last day of the cycle bingyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> On the last day of the cycle bingyin there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 執金吾朱浮上疏曰：「昔堯、舜之盛，猶如三考；

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice Zhu Fu submitted a memorial: "In former times, even in the flourishing of Yao and Shun, there was still the three examinations;
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Zhu Fu memorialized: "Even Yao and Shun at their height required three years of trial;"

sentences.zh: 大漢之興，亦累功效，吏皆積久，至長子孫。

translations.literal: "the great Han's rise also accumulated merit through many terms; clerks all served long, until sons and grandsons succeeded."
translations.idiomatic: "Han too rose through long service; officers held office for years until sons and grandsons inherited their posts."

sentences.zh: 當時吏職，何能悉治，論議之徒，豈不喧嘩！

translations.literal: "At that time how could every official post be fully governed? Would not the faction of disputants have clamored!"
translations.idiomatic: "Could every post have been perfectly filled then? Would critics not have roared?"

sentences.zh: 蓋以為天地之功不可倉卒，艱難之業當累日也。

translations.literal: "Surely because the work of Heaven and earth cannot be rushed, and arduous enterprise must accumulate through days."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's work cannot be rushed; great undertakings need time."

sentences.zh: 而間者守宰數見換易，迎新相代，疲勞道路。

translations.literal: "Yet recently prefects and magistrates have repeatedly been replaced; welcoming the new and handing on to the next, the roads are worn with fatigue."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet lately prefects and magistrates are swapped again and again—welcoming the new, seeing off the old—until the roads groan with their comings and goings."

sentences.zh: 尋其視事日淺，未足昭見其職，既加嚴切，人不自保，迫於舉劾，懼於刺譏，故爭飾詐偽以希虛譽，斯所以致日月失行之應也。

translations.literal: "Search out their days in office—they are short, insufficient to make their duties manifest. Since strictness was added, men cannot preserve themselves; pressed by impeachment, fearful of censure and exposure, they therefore compete to adorn fraud and falsehood hoping for empty praise—this is what brings the response of sun and moon losing their course."
translations.idiomatic: "They barely take office before they are moved on, with no time to prove themselves. Under harsh scrutiny men cannot stand secure; hunted by impeachment, dreading exposure, they vie to paint false fronts for hollow praise—and that brings the sun and moon out of their course."

sentences.zh: 夫物暴長者必夭折，功卒成者必亟壞。

translations.literal: "Things that shoot up violently must perish young; achievements finished in a rush must soon break."
translations.idiomatic: "What shoots up too fast must die young; what is finished in haste must soon crack."

sentences.zh: 如摧長久之業而造速成之功，非陛下之福也。

translations.literal: "To dash long-standing enterprise and forge quick-completion achievement is not Your Majesty's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: "To tear down long work for quick results is no blessing to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 願陛下遊意於經年之外，望治於一世之後，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: "I wish Your Majesty would let your mind roam beyond mere years and look for good order after a whole age—the realm would be greatly blessed!"
translations.idiomatic: "May Your Majesty set your mind on years ahead and look for order after a generation—the realm would be blessed indeed!"

sentences.zh: 」帝采其言，自是牧守易代頗簡。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted his words; from this the replacement of governors and defenders became rather sparing.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his counsel; thereafter provincial appointments changed less often.

sentences.zh: 9〔冬〕，十二月<ref>〔冬〕十二月據《通鑑》通例補「冬」字。

translations.literal: 9. 〔Winter〕, the twelfth month<ref>〔Winter〕—the character "winter" for the twelfth month is supplied per the Comprehensive Mirror's usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: 9. 〔Winter〕, the twelfth month<ref>〔Winter〕—"winter" is supplied for the twelfth month per the Comprehensive Mirror's usual practice.

sentences.zh: </ref>，壬辰，大司空宋弘免。

translations.literal: </ref> On the day renchen, Grand Minister of Works Song Hong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> On renchen day Grand Minister of Works Song Hong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 10癸巳，詔曰：「頃者師旅未解，用度不足，故行十一之稅。

translations.literal: 10. On the day guisi, an edict said: "Recently armies and campaigns were not yet concluded; expenditures were insufficient—therefore the tax of one in eleven was imposed."
translations.idiomatic: 10. On guisi day an edict said: "While armies were still in the field and funds ran short, we levied one part in eleven."

sentences.zh: 今糧儲差積，其令郡國收見田租三十稅一，如舊制。

translations.literal: "Now grain stores have somewhat accumulated; let commanderies and kingdoms collect the present field tax at one in thirty, as the old statute."
translations.idiomatic: "Stores have begun to fill again. Let commanderies and kingdoms collect the field tax at one part in thirty, as of old."

sentences.zh: 11諸將之下隴也，帝詔耿弇軍漆，馮異軍栒邑，祭遵軍汧，吳漢等還屯長安。

translations.literal: 11. When the generals came down from Long, the emperor ordered Geng Yan's army to Qi, Feng Yi's army to Xunyi, Ji Zun's army to Qian, and Wu Han and others to return and encamp at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: 11. When the generals retreated from Long, the emperor posted Geng Yan at Qi, Feng Yi at Xunyi, Ji Zun at Qian, and Wu Han and the rest at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 馮異引軍未至栒邑，隗囂乘勝使王元、行巡將二萬餘人下隴，分遣巡取栒邑。

translations.literal: Feng Yi was leading his army but had not yet reached Xunyi when Wei Xiao, riding victory, sent Wang Yuan and Xing Xun with more than twenty thousand men down from Long, dispatching Xun in a separate detachment to take Xunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi had not yet reached Xunyi when Wei Xiao, pressing his advantage, sent Wang Yuan and Xing Xun with more than twenty thousand men down from Long, and detached Xun to seize Xunyi.

sentences.zh: 異即馳兵欲先據之，諸將曰：「虜兵盛而乘勝，不可與爭鋒，宜止軍便地，徐思方略。

translations.literal: Yi immediately spurred his troops wishing to seize it first; the generals said: "The enemy's soldiers are numerous and riding victory—we cannot contend at the spearhead; we ought to halt the army on favorable ground and slowly devise strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi spurred his men to seize the city first. His officers said, "The enemy is strong and riding victory. We cannot meet them head-on. Halt on good ground and plan."

sentences.zh: 」異曰：「虜兵臨境，忸心犬小利，遂欲深入；

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The enemy's troops press the border, their hearts accustomed like dogs to small gain, and they wish at once to drive deep;
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Yi said, "The enemy is at our border, their hearts craven as dogs after small gain, and they mean to drive deep;"

sentences.zh: 若得栒邑，三輔動搖。

translations.literal: "if they gain Xunyi, the Three Metropolises will shake."
translations.idiomatic: "if they take Xunyi, the Three Metropolises will shake."

sentences.zh: 夫攻者不足，守者有餘。

translations.literal: "In attack the force is insufficient; in defense the defender has surplus."
translations.idiomatic: "Attack lacks strength; defense has surplus."

sentences.zh: 今先據城，以逸待勞，非所以爭也。

translations.literal: "Now to seize the city first, awaiting with ease their weariness—this is not the way to contend."
translations.idiomatic: "Seize the city first and meet them fresh while they are weary—that is not contention at all."

sentences.zh: 」潛往，閉城，偃旗鼓。

translations.literal: " He went secretly, closed the city, and lowered banners and drums.
translations.idiomatic: " He went in secret, shut the city, and lowered banners and drums.

sentences.zh: 行巡不知，馳赴之。

translations.literal: Xing Xun did not know and galloped to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Xun did not know and galloped there.

sentences.zh: 異乘其不意，卒擊鼓、建旗而出。

translations.literal: Yi seized their lack of expectation, suddenly beat drums and raised banners, and sallied out.
translations.idiomatic: Yi caught them off guard, suddenly beat drums, raised banners, and sallied out.

sentences.zh: 巡軍驚亂奔走，追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xun's army panicked, scattered, and fled; they pursued and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's army panicked and fled; they pursued and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 祭遵亦破王元於汧。

translations.literal: Ji Zun also defeated Wang Yuan at Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zun also defeated Wang Yuan at Qian.

sentences.zh: 於是北地諸豪長耿定等悉畔隗囂降。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the powerful men and elders of Beidi, including Geng Ding, entirely turned from Wei Ao and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the powerful men and elders of Beidi, including Geng Ding, turned from Wei Ao and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔異進軍義渠，擊破盧芳將賈覽、匈奴奧鞬日逐王，北地、上郡、安定皆降。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi to advance the army to Yiqu, defeated Lu Fang's general Jia Lan and the Xiongnu Ao Jian Rizhu King; Beidi, Shang, and Anding all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yi to advance to Yiqu, defeated Lu Fang's general Jia Lan and the Xiongnu Ao Jian Rizhu King, and Beidi, Shang, and Anding all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 12竇融復遣其弟友上書曰：「臣幸得托先後末屬，累世二千石，臣復假歷將帥，守持一隅，故遣劉鈞口陳肝膽，自以底裡上露，長無纖介。

translations.literal: 12 Dou Rong again sent his younger brother You to present a memorial, saying: "Your servant was fortunate to rely on attachment to the former and latter imperial houses, for generations held the two-thousand-bushel offices; your servant again was lent successive service as commander, holding one corner, and therefore sent Liu Jun to state heart and liver by mouth, taking it that my inmost self was laid bare above and would long be without the slightest flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong again sent his younger brother You to present a memorial, saying: "I was fortunate to rely on attachment to the former and latter imperial houses; my family for generations held two-thousand-bushel offices; I have again served as commander and held one corner, and therefore sent Liu Jun to speak my heart openly, believing my inmost loyalty was laid bare and would long remain without the slightest flaw.

sentences.zh: 而璽書盛稱蜀、漢二主三分鼎足之權，任囂、尉佗之謀，竊自痛傷。

translations.literal: Yet the imperial letter lavishly praised the two lords of Shu and Han and the power to divide the realm like a tripod cauldron, the schemes of Ren Xiao and Wei Tuo—I privately was pained and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial letter lavishly praised the two lords of Shu and Han and the power to divide the realm like a tripod, the schemes of Ren Xiao and Wei Tuo—and I was privately pained and wounded.

sentences.zh: 臣融雖無識，猶知利害之際、順逆之分。

translations.literal: Your servant Rong, though without understanding, still knows the juncture of benefit and harm and the distinction of compliance and defiance.
translations.idiomatic: I, Rong, though without great understanding, still know the juncture of benefit and harm and the distinction of compliance and defiance.

sentences.zh: 豈可背真舊之主，事奸偽之人；

translations.literal: How could one turn against the true former lord and serve treacherous, false men;
translations.idiomatic: How could one turn against the true former lord and serve treacherous, false men;

sentences.zh: 廢忠貞小節，為傾覆之事；

translations.literal: abandon the small integrity of loyalty and constancy and do deeds of overthrow;
translations.idiomatic: abandon the small integrity of loyalty and constancy and do deeds of overthrow;

sentences.zh: 棄已成之基，求無冀之利。

translations.literal: cast away an already completed foundation and seek profit without hope.
translations.idiomatic: cast away an already completed foundation and seek profit without hope.

sentences.zh: 此三者，雖問狂夫，猶知去就，而臣獨何以用心！

translations.literal: These three—though one asked a madman, he would still know departure and approach—yet why alone should your servant set his mind on them!
translations.idiomatic: These three—even a madman would know what to accept and reject—so why alone should I set my mind on them!

sentences.zh: 謹遣弟友詣闕，口陳至誠。

translations.literal: I respectfully send my younger brother You to the palace gate to state utmost sincerity by mouth.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully send my younger brother You to court to speak my utmost sincerity in person.

sentences.zh: 」友至高平，會隗囂反，道不通，乃遣司馬席封間道通書。

translations.literal: " You reached Gaoping; it happened that Wei Ao rebelled and the road was not open, so he sent Marshal Xi Feng by a secret path to deliver the letter.
translations.idiomatic: " You reached Gaoping, but Wei Ao had rebelled and the road was blocked, so he sent Marshal Xi Feng by a secret path to deliver the letter.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣封，賜融、友書，所以尉藉之甚厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Feng back, bestowing letters on Rong and You—the means by which he comforted and reassured them were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent Feng back with letters for Rong and You, comforting and reassuring them very generously.

sentences.zh: 融乃與隗囂書曰：「將軍親遇厄會之際，國家不利之時，守節不回，承事本朝。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon wrote to Wei Ao, saying: "General, you personally met the juncture of calamity and the time when the state was unfavored, held your integrity without turning back, and continued to serve the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then wrote to Wei Ao, saying: "General, you personally met calamity and a time when the state was unfavored, held your integrity without turning back, and continued to serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 融等所以欣服高義，願從役於將軍者，良為此也！

translations.literal: The reason Rong and the others rejoiced in and submitted to your lofty righteousness and wished to follow and serve under the general is truly for this!
translations.idiomatic: The reason we rejoiced in your lofty righteousness and wished to serve under you is truly this!

sentences.zh: 而忿悁之間，改節易圖，委成功，造難就，百年累之，一朝毀之，豈不惜乎！

translations.literal: Yet in a moment of anger you changed your integrity and altered your plan, abandoned success and created difficulty, what a hundred years had built up you destroyed in a morning—is it not to be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a moment of anger you changed your integrity and altered your plan, abandoned success and created difficulty, destroyed in a morning what a hundred years had built—is that not to be regretted!

sentences.zh: 殆執事者貪功建謀，以至於此。

translations.literal: Perhaps those in charge, greedy for achievement, devised the plot and brought things to this.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps those in charge, greedy for achievement, devised the plot and brought things to this.

sentences.zh: 當今西州地勢局迫，民兵離散，易以輔人，難以自建。

translations.literal: Now the Western Province's terrain is cramped and pressing, militia and people scattered—it is easy to assist others and hard to stand on one's own.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Western Province is cramped, its militia and people scattered—it is easy to assist others and hard to stand on one's own.

sentences.zh: 計若失路不反，聞道猶迷，不南合子陽，則北入文伯耳。

translations.literal: If the plan loses the road and does not return, hears the Way yet is still lost—if you do not join Ziyang in the south, then you will enter Wenbo in the north.
translations.idiomatic: If you lose the road and do not return, hear the Way yet remain lost—if you do not join Ziyang in the south, you will go to Wenbo in the north.

sentences.zh: 夫負虛交而易強禦，恃遠救而輕近敵，未見其利也。

translations.literal: To bear empty friendship and lightly oppose the strong, to rely on distant rescue and slight a near enemy—its benefit is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: To rely on empty friendship and lightly oppose the strong, to count on distant rescue and slight a near enemy—its benefit is not seen.

sentences.zh: 自兵起以來，城郭皆為丘墟，生民轉於溝壑。

translations.literal: Since troops rose, city walls and moats have all become mounds and ruins; the living people have been cast into ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began, cities have become ruins and the people cast into ditches and gullies.

sentences.zh: 幸賴天運少還，而將軍復重其難，是使積痾不得遂瘳，幼孤將復流離，言之可為酸鼻。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on Heaven's movement to return a little, yet the general again doubles the hardship—this makes accumulated illness unable to be healed at last, infants and orphans about to be cast adrift again; to speak of it can make the nose sting with sour grief.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Heaven's favor has begun to return, yet the general again doubles the hardship—this keeps accumulated ills from healing and will cast infants and orphans adrift again; to speak of it is heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 庸人且猶不忍，況仁者乎！

translations.literal: Even a mediocre man could not bear it—how much more a benevolent man!
translations.idiomatic: Even a mediocre man could not bear it—how much more a benevolent man!

sentences.zh: 融聞為忠甚易，得宜實難。

translations.literal: Rong has heard that doing loyalty is very easy, but obtaining what is fitting is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that doing loyalty is easy, but obtaining what is fitting is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 憂人太過，以德取怨，知且以言獲罪也！

translations.literal: Worrying for others too much, by virtue one draws resentment—I know I shall yet be punished by words!
translations.idiomatic: To worry for others too much is to draw resentment by one's virtue—I know I shall yet be punished for these words!

sentences.zh: 」囂不納。

translations.literal: " Ao did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Ao did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 融乃與五郡太守共砥厲兵馬，上疏請師期；

translations.literal: Rong thereupon together with the five commandery governors jointly sharpened troops and horses and presented a memorial requesting a date for the army;
translations.idiomatic: Rong then together with the five commandery governors sharpened troops and horses and memorialized requesting a date for the army;

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉美之。

translations.literal: the Emperor deeply praised and admired it.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor deeply praised it.

sentences.zh: 融即與諸郡守將兵入金城，擊囂黨先零羌封何等，大破之。

translations.literal: Rong immediately together with the various commandery governors led troops into Jincheng, struck Ao's faction the Qiang of Xianling Feng He and others, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rong immediately led the commandery governors with troops into Jincheng, struck Ao's allies the Xianling Qiang Feng He and others, and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 因並河，揚威武，伺候車駕。

translations.literal: He thereupon followed the river, displayed martial might, and awaited the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the river, displayed martial might, and awaited the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 時大兵未進，融乃引還。

translations.literal: At the time the great army had not advanced; Rong thereupon withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The great army had not yet advanced, so Rong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝以融信效著明，益嘉之，修理融父墳墓，祠以太牢，數馳輕使，致遺四方珍羞。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Rong's faith and achievement were clearly outstanding, praised him the more, repaired Rong's father's tomb, sacrificed to it with the great offering, and repeatedly sent swift envoys bearing gifts of rare delicacies from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rong's faith and achievement were clearly outstanding, the Emperor praised him further, repaired his father's tomb, sacrificed to it with the great offering, and repeatedly sent swift envoys bearing rare delicacies from the four directions.

sentences.zh: 梁統猶恐眾心疑惑，乃使人刺殺張玄，遂與隗囂絕，皆解所假將軍印綬。

translations.literal: Liang Tong still feared the host's hearts were doubtful; he then had men assassinate Zhang Xuan, thereupon broke with Wei Ao, and all surrendered the borrowed general's seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tong still feared the troops were doubtful; he had Zhang Xuan assassinated, broke with Wei Ao, and all surrendered their borrowed general's seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 13先是，馬援聞隗囂欲貳於漢，數以書責譬之，囂得書增怒。

translations.literal: 13 Earlier, Ma Yuan heard that Wei Ao wished to waver toward Han and repeatedly by letter reproached and admonished him; Ao received the letters and grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ma Yuan heard that Wei Ao wished to waver toward Han and repeatedly reproached him by letter; Ao grew angrier with each letter.

sentences.zh: 及囂發兵反，援乃上書曰：「臣與隗囂本實交友，初遣臣東，謂臣曰：『本欲為漢，願足下往觀之，於汝意可，即專心矣。

translations.literal: When Ao raised troops and rebelled, Yuan thereupon presented a memorial, saying: "Your servant and Wei Ao were in truth friends; when he first sent your servant east he said to me: 'Originally I wished to serve Han; I hope you, sir, will go observe; if it suits your mind, then devote yourself wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ao raised troops and rebelled, Yuan presented a memorial, saying: "Wei Ao and I were truly friends; when he first sent me east he said to me: 'Originally I wished to serve Han; I hope you will go observe; if it suits your mind, then devote yourself wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 』及臣還反，報以赤心，實欲導之於善，非敢譎以非義。

translations.literal: ' When your servant returned and reported with a red heart, he truly wished to guide him toward the good and did not dare deceive with what was not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: ' When I returned and reported with a loyal heart, I truly wished to guide him toward the good and did not dare deceive him with what was not righteous.

sentences.zh: 而囂自挾奸心，盜憎主人，怨毒之情，遂歸於臣。

translations.literal: Yet Ao on his own harbored a treacherous heart, hated his master like a thief, and the feeling of resentful poison thereupon turned upon your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ao on his own harbored treachery, hated his master like a thief, and his resentful poison turned upon me.

sentences.zh: 臣欲不言，則無以上聞，願聽詣行在所，極陳滅囂之術。

translations.literal: Your servant wished not to speak, yet then there would be nothing to report above; I wish to be permitted to go to the traveling palace and set forth to the utmost the art of destroying Ao.
translations.idiomatic: If I wished not to speak, there would be nothing to report above; I ask permission to go to the traveling palace and set forth fully the art of destroying Ao.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃召之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon summoned him.

sentences.zh: 援具言謀畫。

translations.literal: Yuan fully stated plans and designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan fully stated his plans.

sentences.zh: 帝因使援將突騎五千，往來遊說囂將高峻、任禹之屬，下及羌豪，為陳禍福，以離囂支黨。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon had Yuan lead five thousand shock cavalry, go back and forth to persuade Ao's generals Gao Jun, Ren Yu, and their kind, down to the Qiang chieftains, set forth fortune and calamity for them, and thereby divide Ao's supporting factions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Yuan lead five thousand shock cavalry, go back and forth persuading Ao's generals Gao Jun, Ren Yu, and their kind, down to the Qiang chieftains, set forth fortune and calamity, and thereby divide Ao's supporters.

sentences.zh: 援又為書與囂將楊廣，使曉勸於囂曰：「援竊見四海已定，兆民同情，而季孟閉拒背畔，為天下表的。

translations.literal: Yuan also wrote a letter to Ao's general Yang Guang, to have him enlighten and urge Ao, saying: "Yuan has privately seen that within the four seas is settled, the myriad people share one feeling, yet Jimeng shuts himself off, refuses, and turns his back—he is a model for the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also wrote to Ao's general Yang Guang to enlighten and urge Ao, saying: "I have privately seen that within the four seas is settled and the myriad people share one feeling, yet Jimeng shuts himself off and rebels—he is a model for the world.

sentences.zh: 常懼海內切齒，思相屠裂，故遺書戀戀，以致惻隱之計。

translations.literal: I constantly fear that within the seas people grind their teeth and think of slaughtering one another; therefore I sent letters full of longing to offer a plan of compassionate pity.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly fear that within the seas people grind their teeth and think of slaughtering one another; therefore I sent letters full of longing to offer a plan of compassionate pity.

sentences.zh: 乃聞季孟歸罪於援，而納王游翁諂邪之說，因自謂函谷以西，舉足可定。

translations.literal: Yet I hear that Jimeng lays the blame on Yuan and accepts the flattery and wickedness of Wang Youweng's words, and therefore thinks that west of Hangu Pass, wherever he sets foot can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that Jimeng lays the blame on me and accepts the flattery and wickedness of Wang Youweng's words, and therefore thinks that west of Hangu Pass he can settle everything wherever he sets foot.

sentences.zh: 以今而觀，竟何如邪！

translations.literal: Viewed from today—how does it turn out after all!
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from today—how does it turn out after all!

sentences.zh: 援間至河內，過存伯春，見其奴吉從西方還，說伯春小弟仲舒望見吉，欲問伯春無它否，竟不能言，曉夕號泣，宛轉塵中。

translations.literal: Yuan by chance reached Henei, passed to inquire after Bochun, saw his slave Ji returning from the west, who said Bochun's younger brother Zhongshu, seeing Ji from afar, wished to ask whether Bochun was without other trouble, yet in the end could not speak, wept morning and evening, and writhed in the dust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan by chance reached Henei and called on Bochun; he saw his slave Ji returning from the west, who said Bochun's younger brother Zhongshu, seeing Ji from afar, wished to ask whether Bochun was safe, yet could not speak, wept morning and evening, and writhed in the dust.

sentences.zh: 又說其家悲愁之狀，不可言也。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the grief and sorrow of his household—unspeakable.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of his household's grief and sorrow—unspeakable.

sentences.zh: 夫怨讎可刺不可毀，援聞之，不自知泣下也。

translations.literal: A foe of resentment may be stabbed but not destroyed; Yuan heard it and, without knowing it, wept.
translations.idiomatic: A foe of resentment may be stabbed but not destroyed; when Yuan heard it he wept without knowing it.

sentences.zh: 援素知季孟孝愛，曾、閔不過。

translations.literal: Yuan has long known Jimeng's filial love—not surpassed by Zeng and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan has long known Jimeng's filial love—not surpassed by Zeng and Min.

sentences.zh: 夫孝於其親，豈不慈於其子！

translations.literal: If one is filial toward one's parents, how could one not be loving toward one's sons!
translations.idiomatic: If one is filial toward one's parents, how could one not be loving toward one's sons!

sentences.zh: 可有子抱三木而跳梁妄作，自同分羹之事乎！

translations.literal: Can there be a son who bears the triple cangue and capers in reckless rebellion, making himself the same as the affair of dividing the broth!
translations.idiomatic: Can there be a son who bears the cangue and capers in reckless rebellion, making himself the same as the affair of dividing the broth!

sentences.zh: 季孟平生自言所以擁兵眾者，欲以保全父母之國而完墳墓也，又言苟厚士大夫而已。

translations.literal: Jimeng in his life has himself said that the reason he gathered a host was to wish to preserve his parents' state and complete the tombs, and again said he wished only to treat scholars generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jimeng has himself said that the reason he gathered troops was to preserve his parents' state and complete the tombs, and that he wished only to treat scholars generously.

sentences.zh: 而今所欲全者將破亡之，所欲完者將毀傷之，所欲厚者將反薄之。

translations.literal: Yet now what he wished to preserve will be destroyed and perish, what he wished to complete will be ruined and harmed, what he wished to treat generously will instead be treated thinly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now what he wished to preserve will be destroyed, what he wished to complete will be ruined, what he wished to treat generously will instead be treated thinly.

sentences.zh: 季孟嘗折愧子陽而不受其爵，今更共陸陸欲往附之，將難為顏乎！

translations.literal: Jimeng once humbled Ziyang in rebuke and did not accept his rank; now he again together, step by step, wishes to go attach to him—will it not be hard for the face!
translations.idiomatic: Jimeng once humbled Ziyang in rebuke and did not accept his rank; now he again wishes to go attach to him step by step—will that not be hard on his face!

sentences.zh: 若復責以重質，當安從得子主給是哉！

translations.literal: If again charged with heavy hostage, from where will he obtain a lord-son to supply this!
translations.idiomatic: If again charged with heavy hostages, from where will he obtain a lord's son to supply them!

sentences.zh: 往時子陽獨欲以王相待而春卿拒之，今者歸老，更欲低頭與小兒曹共槽櫪而食，並肩側身於怨家之朝乎！

translations.literal: In former times Ziyang alone wished to treat him as king and Chunqing refused; now, returning in old age, he again wishes to bow his head and with little boys share manger and trough to eat, shoulder to shoulder and body to body in the court of his enemy!
translations.idiomatic: In former times Ziyang alone wished to treat him as king and Chunqing refused; now, in old age, he again wishes to bow his head and with little boys share manger and trough, shoulder to shoulder in his enemy's court!

sentences.zh: 今國家待春卿意深，宜使牛孺卿與諸耆老大人共說季孟，若計畫不從，真可引領去矣。

translations.literal: Now the state treats Chunqing's intent deeply; you ought to have Niu Ruqing together with the various elders and great men jointly persuade Jimeng—if the plan is not followed, truly one may stretch the neck and go.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state treats Chunqing with deep intent; you ought to have Niu Ruqing together with the various elders jointly persuade Jimeng—if the plan is not followed, truly one may stretch the neck and go.

sentences.zh: 前披輿地圖，見天下郡國百有六所，奈何欲以區區二邦以當諸夏百有四乎！

translations.literal: Earlier I spread the carriage-map and saw that the empire's commanderies and kingdoms number a hundred and six—how can one wish to use a mere two states to match the hundred and four of all Xia!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I spread the carriage-map and saw that the empire's commanderies and kingdoms number a hundred and six—how can one wish to use a mere two states to match the hundred and four of all Xia!

sentences.zh: 春卿事季孟，外有君臣之義，內有朋友之道。

translations.literal: Chunqing serves Jimeng—outwardly there is the righteousness of ruler and minister, inwardly there is the Way of friends.
translations.idiomatic: Chunqing serves Jimeng—outwardly there is the righteousness of ruler and minister, inwardly there is the Way of friends.

sentences.zh: 言君臣邪，固當諫爭；

translations.literal: Speaking as ruler and minister—certainly one ought to remonstrate and contend;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking as ruler and minister—certainly one ought to remonstrate;

sentences.zh: 語朋友邪，應有切磋。

translations.literal: speaking as friends—there ought to be grinding and polishing.
translations.idiomatic: speaking as friends—there ought to be mutual polishing.

sentences.zh: 豈有知其無成，而但萎腇咋舌，義手從族乎！

translations.literal: How can there be knowing he has no success, yet only shrinking and stammering, folding arms and following the clan!
translations.idiomatic: How can one know he has no success, yet only shrink and stammer, fold one's arms and follow the clan!

sentences.zh: 及今成計，殊尚善也，過是，欲少味矣！

translations.literal: To achieve the plan by today is especially still good; past that, one will wish for a little less flavor!
translations.idiomatic: To achieve the plan today is especially still good; past that, it will lose much of its savor!

sentences.zh: 且來君叔天下信士，朝廷重之，其意依依，常獨為西州言。

translations.literal: Moreover Lai Junshu is a man of trust throughout the world; the court values him; his intent is lingering and constant; he alone often speaks for the Western Province.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lai Junshu is trusted throughout the world; the court values him; his intent is constant; he alone often speaks for the Western Province.

sentences.zh: 援商朝廷，尤欲立信於此，必不負約。

translations.literal: Yuan has discussed with the court; they especially wish to establish trust here and will certainly not break the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: I have discussed with the court; they especially wish to establish trust here and will certainly not break the covenant.

sentences.zh: 援不得久留，願急賜報。

translations.literal: Yuan cannot long remain; I wish you would urgently grant a reply.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot long remain; I wish you would urgently grant a reply.

sentences.zh: 」廣竟不答。

translations.literal: " Guang in the end did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang in the end did not reply.

sentences.zh: 諸將每有疑議，更請呼援，咸敬重焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the generals had doubtful points in discussion, they again requested Yuan be called—they all respected and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the generals had doubtful points, they again requested Yuan be called—they all respected him.

sentences.zh: 14隗囂上疏謝曰：「吏民聞大兵卒至，驚恐自救，臣囂不能禁止。

translations.literal: 14 Wei Ao presented a memorial of apology, saying: "Officials and people, hearing the great army suddenly arrive, were frightened and sought to save themselves—your servant Ao could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ao presented a memorial of apology, saying: "Officials and people, hearing the great army suddenly arrive, were frightened and sought to save themselves—I could not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 兵有大利，不敢廢臣子之節，親自追還。

translations.literal: The troops had great advantage; I did not dare abandon the integrity of a subject and minister, and personally pursued and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had great advantage; I did not dare abandon the integrity of a subject and minister and personally pursued and brought them back.

sentences.zh: 昔虞舜事父，大杖則走，小杖則受，臣雖不敏，敢忘斯義！

translations.literal: Formerly Shun served his father: with a great staff he fled, with a small staff he accepted it—your servant, though not keen, dares forget this righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shun served his father: with a great staff he fled, with a small staff he accepted it—I, though not keen, dare not forget this righteousness!

sentences.zh: 今臣之事，在於本朝，賜死則死，加刑則刑；

translations.literal: Now your servant's affair lies with the dynasty—if death is granted then die, if punishment is added then suffer punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Now my affair lies with the dynasty—if death is granted then I die, if punishment is added then I suffer it;

sentences.zh: 如更得洗心，死骨不朽。

translations.literal: if again permitted to wash the heart, dead bones would not decay.
translations.idiomatic: if again permitted to wash my heart, even dead bones would not decay.

sentences.zh: 」有司以囂言慢，請誅其子。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices, because Ao's words were insolent, requested execution of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices, because Ao's words were insolent, requested execution of his sons.

translations.literal: The Emperor could not bear it and again sent Lai Xi to Qian, bestowing on Ao a letter, saying: "Formerly General Chai said: 'Your Majesty is broad and benevolent; though feudal lords have fled in rebellion and afterward returned, their ranks and titles are at once restored and they are not executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor could not bear it and again sent Lai Xi to Qian with a letter for Ao, saying: "Formerly General Chai said: 'Your Majesty is broad and benevolent; though feudal lords have fled in rebellion and afterward returned, their ranks and titles are at once restored and they are not executed.

sentences.zh: 』今若束手，復遣恂弟歸闕庭者，則爵祿獲全，有浩大之福矣！

translations.literal: ' Now if you bind your hands and again send Xun's younger brother back to the court, then rank and stipend will be wholly preserved and there will be vast blessing!
translations.idiomatic: ' Now if you bind your hands and again send Xun's younger brother back to court, then rank and stipend will be wholly preserved and there will be vast blessing!

sentences.zh: 吾年垂四十，在兵中十歲，厭浮語虛辭。

translations.literal: I am nearly forty, ten years in the army—I am weary of floating words and empty phrases.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly forty, ten years in the army—I am weary of empty phrases.

sentences.zh: 即不欲，勿報。

translations.literal: If you do not wish it, do not reply.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not wish it, do not reply.

sentences.zh: 」囂知帝審其詐，遂遣使稱臣於公孫述。

translations.literal: " Ao knew the Emperor had penetrated his deceit and thereupon sent envoys to declare himself a subject to Gongsun Shu.
translations.idiomatic: " Ao knew the Emperor had penetrated his deceit and sent envoys to declare himself a subject to Gongsun Shu.

sentences.zh: 15匈奴與盧芳為寇不息，帝令歸德侯颯使匈奴以修舊好。

translations.literal: 15 The Xiongnu together with Lu Fang raided without cease; the Emperor ordered Marquis of Guide Sa as envoy to the Xiongnu to restore the old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu together with Lu Fang raided without cease; the Emperor ordered Marquis of Guide Sa as envoy to the Xiongnu to restore the old friendship.

sentences.zh: 單于驕倨，雖遣使報命，而寇暴如故。

translations.literal: The chanyu was arrogant and insolent; though he sent envoys to return the mission, plunder and violence were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu was arrogant; though he sent envoys to return the mission, plunder and violence continued as before.

sentences.zh: 1春，三月，罷郡國輕車、騎士、材官，今還復民伍。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the third month, the commanderies' and kingdoms' light chariots, knights, and materiel officers were dismissed and ordered to return to the common people's companies.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, the commanderies' and kingdoms' light chariots, knights, and materiel officers were dismissed and ordered to return to the common people's companies.

sentences.zh: 2公孫述立隗囂為朔寧王，遣兵往來，為之援勢。

translations.literal: 2 Gongsun Shu established Wei Ao as King of Shuoning, sent troops back and forth, and made supporting momentum for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu established Wei Ao as King of Shuoning, sent troops back and forth, and supported him.

sentences.zh: 3癸亥晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 3 On the last day of guihai, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of guihai there was a solar eclipse.

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials each to present sealed memorials; those who presented memorials might not speak of sageliness; Grand Master of the Palace Zheng Xing presented a memorial, saying: "When the state has no good government, reproof appears in the sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the hundred officials each to present sealed memorials; memorialists might not speak of sageliness; Grand Master of the Palace Zheng Xing presented a memorial, saying: "When the state has no good government, reproof appears in the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 要在因人之心，擇人處位。

translations.literal: The key lies in following people's hearts and choosing men to place in positions.
translations.idiomatic: The key lies in following people's hearts and choosing men to place in positions.

sentences.zh: 今公卿大夫多舉漁陽太守郭人及可大司空者，而不以時定；

translations.literal: Now the high ministers and grand masters mostly recommend Guo Ren, governor of Yuyang, and one fit for Grand Minister of Works, yet do not settle it in good time;
translations.idiomatic: Now the high ministers mostly recommend Guo Ren, governor of Yuyang, and one fit for Grand Minister of Works, yet do not settle it in good time;

sentences.zh: 道路流言，咸曰『朝廷欲用功臣』，功臣用則人位謬矣。

translations.literal: roadside rumor all says 'The court wishes to employ meritorious ministers'—if meritorious ministers are employed, then men's positions are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: roadside rumor says 'The court wishes to employ meritorious ministers'—if meritorious ministers are employed, then men's positions are wrong.

sentences.zh: 願陛下屈己從眾，以濟群臣讓善之功。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would bend yourself and follow the multitude, thereby completing the merit of the ministers yielding what is good.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would bend yourself and follow the multitude, thereby completing the ministers' merit in yielding what is good.

translations.literal: The sun is the image of the ruler and the moon the image of the minister;
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler and the moon the image of the minister;

sentences.zh: 君亢急而臣下促迫，故月行疾。

translations.literal: the ruler is overbearing and urgent while subjects below are pressed and cramped—therefore the moon moves swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: the ruler is overbearing and urgent while subjects below are pressed and cramped—therefore the moon moves swiftly.

sentences.zh: 今陛下高明而群臣惶促，宜留思柔克之政，垂意《洪範》之法。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is lofty and bright while the ministers are fearful and pressed; you ought to ponder long a policy of gentle overcoming, and attend to the methods of the Hong Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is lofty and bright while the ministers are fearful and pressed; you ought to ponder long a policy of gentle overcoming and attend to the methods of the Hong Fan.
