translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor personally attended diligently to government affairs and was rather severe and urgent; therefore Xing's memorial touched on this.

sentences.zh: 4夏，四月，壬午，大赦。

translations.literal: 4 In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 5五月，戊戌，以前將軍李通為大司空。

translations.literal: 5 In the fifth month, on the day wuxu, the former General-in-Chief Li Tong was made Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wuxu, the former General-in-Chief Li Tong was made Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 6大司農江馮上言：「宜令司隸校尉督察三公。

translations.literal: 6 Grand Minister of Agriculture Jiang Feng submitted a memorial: "The Director of the Retainers ought to be ordered to inspect and supervise the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Jiang Feng submitted a memorial: "The Director of the Retainers ought to inspect and supervise the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 」司空掾陳元上疏曰：「臣聞師臣者帝，賓臣者霸。

translations.literal: " Aide to the Minister of Works Chen Yuan submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard: he who has a teacher as minister becomes an emperor; he who has a guest as minister becomes a hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: " Aide to the Minister of Works Chen Yuan submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that a ruler with a teacher as minister becomes an emperor, and one with a guest as minister becomes a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 故武王以太公為師，齊桓以夷吾為仲父，近則高帝優相國之禮，太宗假宰輔之權。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wu of Zhou made Taigong his teacher; Duke Huan of Qi made Yiwu his zhongfu; recently the High Emperor showed exceptional courtesy to the Chancellor, and the Founding Emperor entrusted the chief ministers with full authority.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou made Taigong his teacher; Duke Huan of Qi made Yiwu his zhongfu; recently the High Emperor showed exceptional courtesy to the Chancellor, and Emperor Wen entrusted the chief ministers with full authority.

sentences.zh: 及亡新王莽，遭漢中衰，專操國柄以偷天下，況己自喻，不信群臣，奪公輔之任，損宰相之威，以刺舉為明，徼訐為直，至乃陪僕告其君長，子弟變其父兄，罔密法峻，大臣無所措手足；

translations.literal: When the fallen Xin of Wang Mang met Han in mid-decline, he monopolized the state's handle to steal the realm, moreover took himself as the standard, did not trust his ministers, stripped the Three Excellencies of their duties, diminished the Chancellor's authority, took denunciation and investigation as enlightenment, took petty accusations as uprightness, until attendants and servants denounced their lords and superiors and sons and younger brothers turned against fathers and elder brothers—laws were tangled and severe, and great ministers had nowhere to set hand or foot;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang's fallen Xin met Han in mid-decline, he monopolized state power to steal the realm, prided himself on self-comparison, distrusted his ministers, stripped the Three Excellencies of their duties, diminished the Chancellor's authority, treated denunciation as enlightenment and petty accusations as uprightness, until servants denounced their lords and sons turned against fathers—laws were tangled and severe, and great ministers had nowhere to set hand or foot;

sentences.zh: 然不能禁董忠之謀，身為世戮。

translations.literal: yet he could not suppress Dong Zhong's plot and himself became a slaughter for the age.
translations.idiomatic: yet he could not suppress Dong Zhong's plot and himself became a byword for slaughter.

sentences.zh: 方今四方尚擾，天下未一，百姓觀聽，咸張耳目。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are still disturbed, the realm is not yet one, the common people watch and listen, all stretching eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four quarters are still disturbed, the realm is not yet united, and the common people watch and listen with eyes and ears wide open.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜修文、武之聖典，襲祖宗之遺德，勞心下士，屈節待賢，誠不宜使有司察公輔之名。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to restore the sage canons of Wen and Wu, inherit the legacy virtue of the ancestors, toil in heart to humble yourself before scholars, bend your dignity to await the worthy—it truly is not fitting to let the responsible offices inspect the names of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to restore the sage canons of Wen and Wu, inherit the ancestors' legacy virtue, toil to humble yourself before scholars, and bend your dignity to await the worthy—it is truly not fitting to let the responsible offices inspect the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 7酒泉太守竺曾以弟報怨殺人，自免去郡；

translations.literal: 7 Administrator of Jiuquan Zhu Ceng, because his younger brother killed a man to avenge a grudge, himself resigned and left the commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Jiuquan Zhu Ceng, because his younger brother killed a man to avenge a grudge, resigned and left the commandery;

sentences.zh: 竇融承製拜曾武鋒將軍，更以辛肜為酒泉太守。

translations.literal: Dou Rong by imperial order enfeoffed Ceng as Martial Vanguard General and replaced him with Xin Yin as Administrator of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong by imperial order made Ceng Martial Vanguard General and replaced him with Xin Yin as Administrator of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 8秋，隗囂將步騎三萬侵安定，至陰槃，馮異率諸將拒之；

translations.literal: 8 In autumn Wei Ao led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to invade Anding, reaching Yinpan; Feng Yi led the generals to resist him;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Wei Ao led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to invade Anding and reached Yinpan; Feng Yi led the generals to resist him;

sentences.zh: 囂又令別將下隴攻祭遵於汧。

translations.literal: Ao also ordered a separate general to descend Long and attack Ji Zun at Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ao also ordered a separate general to descend Long and attack Ji Zun at Qian.

sentences.zh: 並無利而還。

translations.literal: Both gained no advantage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Both gained no advantage and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝將自征隗囂，先戒竇融師期，會遇雨，道斷，且囂兵已退，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to campaign in person against Wei Ao and first warned Dou Rong of the army's rendezvous date; he happened to meet rain, roads were cut, and moreover Ao's troops had already withdrawn, and he thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was about to campaign in person against Wei Ao and first warned Dou Rong of the army's rendezvous date; rain cut the roads, Ao's troops had already withdrawn, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝令來歙以書招王遵，遵來降，拜太中大夫，封向義侯。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Lai Xi to recruit Wang Zun by letter; Zun came to surrender, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Lai Xi to recruit Wang Zun by letter; Zun surrendered, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 9冬，盧芳以事誅其五原太守李興兄弟。

translations.literal: 9 In winter Lu Fang on some pretext executed Administrator of Wuyuan Li Xing and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Lu Fang on some pretext executed Administrator of Wuyuan Li Xing and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 其朔方太守田颯、雲中太守喬扈各舉郡降，旁令領職如故。

translations.literal: His Administrators of Shuofang Tian Sa and Yunzhong Qiao Hu each led their commanderies to surrender; the Emperor ordered them to hold their posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: His Administrators of Shuofang Tian Sa and Yunzhong Qiao Hu each led their commanderies to surrender; the Emperor let them hold their posts as before.

sentences.zh: 10帝好圖讖，與鄭興議郊祀事，曰：「吾欲以讖斷之，何如？

translations.literal: 10 The Emperor was fond of prognostic charts and discussed suburban sacrifices with Zheng Xing, saying: "I wish to decide it by omens—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was fond of prognostic charts and discussed suburban sacrifices with Zheng Xing, saying, "I wish to decide it by omens—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不為讖。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant does not produce omens.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I do not produce omens."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「卿不為讖，非之邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor angrily said: "You do not produce omens—you oppose them, do you not?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor angrily said, "You do not produce omens—you oppose them, do you?"

sentences.zh: 」興惶恐曰：「臣於書有所未學，而無所非也。

translations.literal: " Xing in fear said: "Your servant in the classics has what he has not yet studied, but has nothing he rejects.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said in fear, "There are things in the classics I have not yet studied, but nothing I reject."

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃解。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's mood thereupon eased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor's mood thereupon eased.

sentences.zh: 11南陽太守杜詩政治清平，興利除害，百姓便之。

translations.literal: 11 Administrator of Nanyang Du Shi's government was clear and level; he promoted benefit and removed harm, and the common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Nanyang Du Shi's government was clear and fair; he promoted benefit and removed harm, and the common people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 又修治陂池，廣拓土田，郡內比室殷足，時人方於召信臣。

translations.literal: He also repaired dikes and ponds, broadly expanded fields, and within the commandery household after household was well provided; men of the time compared him to Zhaoxin Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He also repaired dikes and ponds and broadly expanded fields; within the commandery household after household was well provided, and men of the time compared him to Zhaoxin Chen.

sentences.zh: 南陽為之語曰：「前有召父，後有杜母。

translations.literal: Nanyang made a saying of it: "Before there was Father Zhao; after there is Mother Du.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang had a saying: "Before there was Father Zhao; after there is Mother Du."

sentences.zh: 1春，來歙將二千餘人伐山開道，從番須、回中徑襲略陽，斬隗囂守將金梁。

translations.literal: 1 In spring Lai Xi led more than two thousand men to cut through mountains and open roads, from Fanxu and Huizhong by a direct path to strike Lueyang, and beheaded Wei Ao's garrison general Jin Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring Lai Xi led more than two thousand men to cut through mountains and open roads, came by Fanxu and Huizhong on a direct path to strike Lueyang, and beheaded Wei Ao's garrison general Jin Liang.

sentences.zh: 囂大驚曰：「何其神也！

translations.literal: Ao was greatly alarmed and said: "How divine!
translations.idiomatic: Ao was greatly alarmed and said, "How divine!"

sentences.zh: 」帝聞得略陽，甚喜，曰：「略陽，囂所依阻。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor heard Lueyang had been taken, he was greatly pleased and said: "Lueyang is what Ao relies on for defense.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor heard Lueyang had been taken, he was greatly pleased and said, "Lueyang is what Ao relies on for defense.

sentences.zh: 心腹已壞，則制其支體易矣！

translations.literal: The heart and belly are already ruined—then controlling his limbs and trunk will be easy!
translations.idiomatic: His heart and belly are already ruined—then controlling his limbs will be easy!"

sentences.zh: 吳漢等諸將聞歙據略陽，爭馳赴之。

translations.literal: The generals Wu Han and the others, hearing Xi held Lueyang, vied to gallop to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wu Han and the others, hearing Xi held Lueyang, all raced to join him.

sentences.zh: 上以為囂失所恃，亡其要城，勢必悉以精銳來攻；

translations.literal: The Emperor thought that Ao had lost what he relied on and lost his key city, and was certain to bring all his elite troops to attack;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought Ao had lost his support and his key city and was certain to bring all his elite troops to attack;

sentences.zh: 曠日久圍而城不拔，士卒頓敝，乃可乘危而進，皆追漢等還。

translations.literal: if the siege dragged on for days without taking the city, the soldiers would be worn and exhausted, and then one could advance on their peril—all were ordered to recall Han and the others.
translations.idiomatic: if the siege dragged on without taking the city the troops would be worn out, and then one could advance on their peril—he ordered Han and the others recalled.

sentences.zh: 隗囂果使王元拒隴坻，行巡守番須口，王孟塞雞頭道，牛邯軍瓦亭。

translations.literal: Wei Ao indeed sent Wang Yuan to hold Longdi, Xing Xun to guard the mouth of Fanxu, Wang Meng to block Jitou Pass, and Niu Han to encamp at Wating.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ao sent Wang Yuan to hold Longdi, Xing Xun to guard the mouth of Fanxu, Wang Meng to block Jitou Pass, and Niu Han to encamp at Wating.

sentences.zh: 囂自悉其大眾數萬人圍略陽，公孫述遣將李育、田弇助之，斬山築堤，激水灌城。

translations.literal: Ao himself mustered his great host of tens of thousands to besiege Lueyang; Gongsun Shu sent generals Li Yu and Tian Yan to assist; they cut mountains and built dikes, channeled water to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ao himself mustered tens of thousands to besiege Lueyang; Gongsun Shu sent Li Yu and Tian Yan to assist; they cut mountains, built dikes, and channeled water to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 來歙與將士固死堅守，矢盡，發屋斷木以為兵。

translations.literal: Lai Xi with the officers and soldiers staunchly held to the death; when arrows were exhausted, they tore apart houses and broke wood to make weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Xi and his officers and soldiers held staunchly to the death; when arrows ran out they tore apart houses and broke wood for weapons.

sentences.zh: 囂盡銳攻之，累月不能下。

translations.literal: Ao exhausted his elite in attacking it for months but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Ao threw all his elite into the attack for months but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏四月，帝自將征隗囂，光祿勳汝南郭憲諫曰：「東方初定，車駕未可遠征。

translations.literal: In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, the Emperor himself led a campaign against Wei Ao; Bearer of the Cap and Scepter Guo Xian of Runan remonstrated, saying: "The east has only just been settled—the imperial carriage must not make a distant campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, the Emperor led a campaign in person against Wei Ao; Bearer of the Cap and Scepter Guo Xian of Runan remonstrated, "The east has only just been settled—the imperial carriage must not campaign so far."

sentences.zh: 」乃當車拔佩刀以斷車靷。

translations.literal: " He thereupon stood before the carriage, drew his girdle-sword, and cut the traces.
translations.idiomatic: " He stood before the carriage, drew his sword, and cut the traces.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，西至漆。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow this and went west as far as Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not listen and went west as far as Qi.

sentences.zh: 諸將多以王師之重，不宜遠入險阻，計冘豫未決；

translations.literal: Many of the generals, on the grounds that the imperial army's weight made it unsuitable to enter far into perilous passes, had plans hesitant and undecided;
translations.idiomatic: Many generals held that the imperial army was too weighty to enter far into perilous passes, and plans were hesitant and undecided;

sentences.zh: 帝召馬援問之。

translations.literal: the Emperor summoned Ma Yuan to question him.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor summoned Ma Yuan to ask his view.

sentences.zh: 援因說隗囂將帥有土崩之勢，兵進有必破之狀；

translations.literal: Yuan thereupon explained that Wei Ao's generals and commanders were in a posture of collapsing like earth, and that if the army advanced there was the certainty of breaking them;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan explained that Wei Ao's generals were on the verge of collapse and that if the army advanced it was certain to break them;

sentences.zh: 又於帝前聚米為山谷，指畫形勢，開示眾軍所從道徑，往來分析，昭然可曉。

translations.literal: moreover before the Emperor he piled rice to make mountains and valleys, traced the terrain, disclosed the routes the host would take, analyzed coming and going, clear and intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: and before the Emperor piled rice into mountains and valleys, traced the terrain, showed the routes the army would take, and analyzed the movements so clearly that all could understand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「虜在吾目中矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The foe is already in my eyes!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The foe is already in my sight!"

sentences.zh: 」明旦，遂進軍，至高平第一。

translations.literal: " The next morning he thereupon advanced the army to Gaoping Di Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " The next morning he advanced the army to Gaoping Di Yi.

sentences.zh: 竇融率五郡太守及羌虜小月氏等步騎數萬，輜重五千餘兩，與大軍會。

translations.literal: Dou Rong led the five commandery administrators and Lesser Yuezhi and other Qiang and barbarian infantry and cavalry numbering tens of thousands, with more than five thousand supply wagons, and joined the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong led the five commandery administrators and Lesser Yuezhi and other Qiang and barbarian infantry and cavalry numbering tens of thousands, with more than five thousand supply wagons, and joined the main army.

sentences.zh: 是時軍旅草創，諸將朝會禮容多不肅，融先遣從事問會見儀適。

translations.literal: At this time the army was newly formed; at court assemblies many generals' ceremonial bearing was not respectful; Rong first sent an attendant to inquire about the proper etiquette for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The army was newly formed; at court assemblies many generals' ceremonial bearing was lax; Rong first sent an attendant to inquire about the proper etiquette for audience.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之，以宣告百僚，乃置酒高會，待融等以殊禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and approved, proclaimed it to the hundred officials, then set out wine for a grand gathering and treated Rong and the others with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and approved, proclaimed it to the hundred officials, set out wine for a grand gathering, and treated Rong and the others with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 遂共進軍，數道上隴。

translations.literal: They thereupon advanced together, on several routes ascending Long.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced together on several routes up Long.

sentences.zh: 使王遵以書招牛邯，下之，拜邯太中大夫。

translations.literal: He had Wang Zun recruit Niu Han by letter; Han submitted, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zun recruited Niu Han by letter; Han submitted and was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 於是囂大將十三人、屬縣十六、眾十餘萬皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirteen of Ao's great generals, sixteen subordinate counties, and a host of more than a hundred thousand all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon thirteen of Ao's great generals, sixteen subordinate counties, and more than a hundred thousand men all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 囂將妻子奔西城，從楊廣，而田弇、李育保上邽。

translations.literal: Ao led his wife and children to flee to Xicheng and followed Yang Guang, while Tian Yan and Li Yu held Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Ao fled with his wife and children to Xicheng and followed Yang Guang, while Tian Yan and Li Yu held Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 略陽圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Lueyang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Lueyang was lifted.

sentences.zh: 帝勞賜來歙，班坐絕席，在諸將之右，賜歙妻縑千匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor rewarded and gifted Lai Xi, seating him on a separate mat apart from the others, to the right of the generals, and gifted Xi's wife a thousand bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded Lai Xi, gave him a separate mat to the right of the generals, and gifted his wife a thousand bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 進幸上邽，詔告隗囂曰：「若束手自詣，父子相見，保無佗也。

translations.literal: He advanced in person to Shanggui and issued an edict telling Wei Ao: "If you bind yourself and come in person, father and son will meet—I guarantee you no other harm.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Shanggui and issued an edict to Wei Ao: "If you bind yourself and come in person, father and son will meet—I guarantee you no other harm."

sentences.zh: 若遂欲為黥布者，亦自任也。

translations.literal: If you persist in wishing to be like Qing Bu, that too is your own choice.
translations.idiomatic: If you persist in being like Qing Bu, that is your own choice."

sentences.zh: 」囂終不降，於是誅其子恂。

translations.literal: " Ao to the end did not surrender; the Emperor thereupon executed his son Xun.
translations.idiomatic: " Ao never surrendered; the Emperor thereupon executed his son Xun.

sentences.zh: 使吳漢、岑彭圍西城，耿弇、蓋延圍上邽。

translations.literal: He sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to besiege Xicheng, Geng Yan and Gai Yan to besiege Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Han and Cen Peng to besiege Xicheng and Geng Yan and Gai Yan to besiege Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 以四縣封竇融為安豐侯，弟友為顯親侯，及五郡太守皆封列侯，遣西還所鎮。

translations.literal: With four counties he enfeoffed Dou Rong as Marquis of Anfeng, his younger brother You as Marquis of Xianqin, and all five commandery administrators were enfeoffed as ranked marquises and sent west to return to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: With four counties he enfeoffed Dou Rong as Marquis of Anfeng and his younger brother You as Marquis of Xianqin; all five commandery administrators were enfeoffed as ranked marquises and sent west to their posts.

sentences.zh: 融以久專方面，懼不自安，數上書求代。

translations.literal: Rong, because he had long held independent authority in his region, feared he could not be secure and several times submitted memorials requesting replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, having long held independent authority in his region, feared for his security and several times asked to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「吾與將軍如左右手耳，數執謙退，何不曉人意！

translations.literal: An edict in reply said: "I and the general are like left and right hands—why again and again hold to modest withdrawal and not understand another's intent!
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "You and I are like left and right hands—why again and again insist on modest withdrawal and not understand my intent!"

sentences.zh: 勉循士民，無擅離部曲！

translations.literal: Urge yourself on in governing scholars and commoners—do not on your own leave your command!
translations.idiomatic: Press on in governing your people—do not leave your command on your own!"

sentences.zh: 穎川盜賊群起，寇沒屬縣，河東守兵亦叛，京師騷動。

translations.literal: Bandits in Yingchuan rose in groups, raided and overran subordinate counties, garrison troops in Hedong also rebelled, and the capital was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Yingchuan rose in groups, raided subordinate counties, garrison troops in Hedong rebelled, and the capital was disturbed.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之曰：「吾悔不用郭子橫之言。

translations.literal: The Emperor, hearing of it, said: "I regret not having used Guo Ziheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I regret not having taken Guo Ziheng's advice."

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，帝自上邽晨夜東馳，賜岑彭等書曰：「兩城若下，便可將兵南擊蜀虜。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, the Emperor from Shanggui day and night galloped east and sent a letter to Cen Peng and the others, saying: "If the two cities fall, you may at once lead troops south to strike the Shu foe.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, the Emperor galloped east day and night from Shanggui and wrote Cen Peng and the others: "If the two cities fall, you may at once lead troops south to strike the Shu foe."

sentences.zh: 人苦不知足，既平隴，復望蜀。

translations.literal: Men suffer from not knowing sufficiency—having pacified Long, they look again to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Men never know sufficiency—having pacified Long, they look again to Shu.

sentences.zh: 每一發兵，頭鬚為白！

translations.literal: Every time troops are dispatched, my hair and beard turn white!
translations.idiomatic: Every time I dispatch troops, my hair and beard turn white!"

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day yimao, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day yimao, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝謂執金吾寇恂曰：「穎川迫近京師，當以時定。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Bearer of the Gilded Mace Kou Xun: "Yingchuan presses close on the capital—it must be settled in good time.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Bearer of the Gilded Mace Kou Xun, "Yingchuan presses close on the capital—it must be settled in good time.

sentences.zh: 惟念獨卿能平之耳，從九卿復出以憂國可也！

translations.literal: I think only you can pacify it—coming forth again from the Nine Ministers to worry for the state is fitting!
translations.idiomatic: I think only you can pacify it—coming forth again from the Nine Ministers for the state's sake is fitting!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「穎川聞陛下有事隴、蜀，故狂狡乘間相詿誤耳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Yingchuan heard Your Majesty was occupied with Long and Shu, so the reckless and cunning took advantage of the interval to mislead one another.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Yingchuan heard Your Majesty was occupied with Long and Shu, so the reckless took advantage of the interval to mislead one another.

sentences.zh: 如聞乘輿南向，賊必惶怖歸死，臣願執銳前驅。

translations.literal: If they hear the imperial carriage is heading south, the bandits are certain to be fearful and return to their deaths; your servant wishes to grasp sharp weapons and lead the van.
translations.idiomatic: If they hear the imperial carriage is heading south, the bandits will be fearful and submit; I wish to take the van with arms in hand."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚申，車駕南征，穎川盜賊悉降。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen the imperial carriage campaigned south; the Yingchuan bandits all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen the imperial carriage campaigned south and the Yingchuan bandits all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 寇恂竟不拜郡，百姓遮道曰：「願從陛下復借寇君一年。

translations.literal: Kou Xun in the end did not accept the commandery; the common people blocked the road, saying: "We wish to beg Your Majesty to lend us Lord Kou for one more year.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun in the end did not take the commandery; the common people blocked the road, saying, "We beg Your Majesty to lend us Lord Kou for one more year."

sentences.zh: 」乃留恂長社，鎮撫吏民，受納餘降。

translations.literal: " He thereupon kept Xun at Changshe to pacify officials and commoners and receive those still surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept Xun at Changshe to pacify officials and commoners and receive those still surrendering.

sentences.zh: 東郡、濟陰盜賊亦起，帝遣李通、王常擊之。

translations.literal: Bandits in Dong and Jiyin also rose; the Emperor sent Li Tong and Wang Chang to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Dong and Jiyin also rose; the Emperor sent Li Tong and Wang Chang to strike them.

sentences.zh: 以東光侯耿純嘗為東郡太守，威信著於衛地，遣使拜太中大夫，使與大兵會東郡。

translations.literal: Because Marquis of Dongguang Geng Chun had once been Administrator of Dong and his authority and trust were established in the lands of Wei, the Emperor sent an envoy to appoint him Grand Master of the Palace and had him join the great army at Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Because Marquis of Dongguang Geng Chun had once been Administrator of Dong and his authority was established in Wei, the Emperor appointed him Grand Master of the Palace and had him join the main army at Dong.

sentences.zh: 東郡聞純入界，盜賊九千餘人皆詣純降，大兵不戰而還；

translations.literal: Dong, hearing Chun had entered its borders, had more than nine thousand bandits all come to Chun to surrender; the great army returned without fighting;
translations.idiomatic: When Dong heard Chun had entered its borders, more than nine thousand bandits all came to him to surrender; the main army returned without fighting;

sentences.zh: 璽書復以純為東郡太守。

translations.literal: an imperial letter again made Chun Administrator of Dong.
translations.idiomatic: an imperial letter again made Chun Administrator of Dong.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，車駕還自穎川。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin the imperial carriage returned from Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin the imperial carriage returned from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 2安丘侯張步將妻子逃奔臨淮，與弟弘、藍欲招其故眾，乘船入海。

translations.literal: 2 Marquis of Anqiu Zhang Bu led his wife and children in flight to Linhuai; with his younger brothers Hong and Lan he wished to rally his former host and take ship to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Anqiu Zhang Bu fled with his wife and children to Linhuai; with his younger brothers Hong and Lan he wished to rally his former followers and take ship to sea.

sentences.zh: 琅邪太守陳俊追討，斬之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Langye Chen Jun pursued and attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Langye Chen Jun pursued and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 3冬，十月，丙午，上行幸懷；

translations.literal: 3 In winter, the tenth month, on the day bingwu, the Emperor went in person to favor Huai;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day bingwu, the Emperor visited Huai;

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙丑，還雒陽。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on the day yichou, he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on the day yichou, he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 4楊廣死，隗囂窮困，其大將王捷別在戎丘，登城呼漢軍曰：「為隗王城守者，皆必死，無二心。

translations.literal: 4 Yang Guang died; Wei Ao was destitute; his great general Wang Jie was separately at Rongqiu, mounted the wall, and called to the Han army: "All who hold the city for King Wei are certain to die—there is no second thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guang died; Wei Ao was destitute; his great general Wang Jie was at Rongqiu, mounted the wall, and called to the Han army, "All who hold the city for King Wei are certain to die—there is no second thought."

sentences.zh: 願諸軍亟罷，請自殺以明之。

translations.literal: I wish the armies to withdraw at once; I request to kill myself to make this clear.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the armies to withdraw at once; I will kill myself to make this clear."

sentences.zh: 」遂自刎死。

translations.literal: " He thereupon cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 初，帝敕吳漢曰：「諸郡甲卒但坐費糧食，若有逃亡，則沮敗眾心，宜悉罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had charged Wu Han: "The armored soldiers of the various commanderies only sit and waste grain; if any flee, they will break the host's hearts—you ought to dismiss them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had charged Wu Han, "The armored soldiers of the various commanderies only sit and waste grain; if any flee they will break the army's heart—you ought to dismiss them all."

sentences.zh: 」漢等貪并力攻囂，遂不能遣，糧食日少，吏士疲役，逃亡者多。

translations.literal: " Han and the others, greedy to combine strength and attack Ao, thereupon could not send them away; grain daily grew less, officials and soldiers were worn by labor, and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Han and the others, greedy to combine strength and attack Ao, could not send them away; grain daily grew less, officials and soldiers were worn by labor, and many fled.

sentences.zh: 岑彭壅谷水灌西城，城未沒丈餘。

translations.literal: Cen Peng dammed the Gu River to flood Xicheng; the city was not yet submerged by more than a zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Peng dammed the Gu River to flood Xicheng; the water had not yet submerged the city by more than a zhang.

sentences.zh: 會王元、行巡、周宗將蜀救兵五千餘人乘高卒至，鼓噪大呼曰：「百萬之眾方至！

translations.literal: Just then Wang Yuan, Xing Xun, and Zhou Zong led more than five thousand Shu relief troops, taking the heights, suddenly arrived, beat drums and shouted loudly: "A host of a million is just arriving!
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Yuan, Xing Xun, and Zhou Zong led more than five thousand Shu relief troops down from the heights, beat drums and shouted, "A host of a million is just arriving!"

sentences.zh: 」漢軍大驚，未及成陳，元等決圍殊死戰，遂得入城，迎囂歸冀。

translations.literal: " The Han army was greatly alarmed, had not yet formed ranks; Yuan and the others broke the encirclement and fought to the death, thereupon were able to enter the city and welcomed Ao back to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han army was greatly alarmed and had not yet formed ranks; Yuan and the others broke the encirclement and fought to the death, entered the city, and welcomed Ao back to Ji.

sentences.zh: 吳漢軍食盡，乃燒輜重，引兵下隴，蓋延、耿弇亦相隨而退。

translations.literal: Wu Han's army's food was exhausted; he thereupon burned the baggage train and led troops down Long; Gai Yan and Geng Yan also followed one another in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han's army ran out of food; he burned the baggage train and led troops down Long; Gai Yan and Geng Yan withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 囂出兵尾擊諸營，岑彭為後拒，諸將乃得全軍東歸；

translations.literal: Ao sent troops to strike the rear of the camps; Cen Peng served as rear guard, and the generals thereupon were able to bring the whole army back east;
translations.idiomatic: Ao sent troops to strike the rear of the camps; Cen Peng served as rear guard and the generals brought the whole army back east;

sentences.zh: 唯祭遵屯汧不退。

translations.literal: only Ji Zun, garrisoned at Qian, did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: only Ji Zun, garrisoned at Qian, did not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 吳漢等復屯長安，岑彭還津鄉。

translations.literal: Wu Han and others again encamped at Chang'an; Cen Peng returned to Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han and others again encamped at Chang'an; Cen Peng returned to Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 於是安定、北地、天水、隴西復反為囂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Anding, Beidi, Tianshui, and Longxi again turned rebel for Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Anding, Beidi, Tianshui, and Longxi again rebelled in support of Wei Ao.

sentences.zh: 校尉太原溫序為囂將苟宇所獲，宇曉譬數四，欲降之。

translations.literal: Commandant Wen Xu of Taiyuan was captured by Ao's general Gou Yu; Yu reasoned and exhorted him four times, wishing to make him submit.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Wen Xu of Taiyuan was captured by Wei Ao's general Gou Yu; Yu reasoned with him four times, wishing to win his surrender.

sentences.zh: 序大怒，叱宇等曰：「虜何敢迫脅漢將！

translations.literal: Xu was greatly angered and shouted at Yu and the others: "How dare you barbarians coerce a Han general!
translations.idiomatic: Xu was greatly angered and shouted at Yu and the others, "How dare you barbarians coerce a Han general!"

sentences.zh: 」因以節廝殺數人。

translations.literal: " He thereupon with his staff of authority hacked and killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon used his staff of authority to hack down and kill several men.

sentences.zh: 宇眾爭欲殺之，宇止之曰：「此義士，死節，可賜以劍。

translations.literal: Yu's host all struggled to kill him; Yu stopped them and said: "This is a man of righteousness who dies for his integrity—he may be granted a sword.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's men all clamored to kill him; Yu stopped them and said, "This is a man of righteousness who dies for his integrity—grant him a sword."

sentences.zh: 」序受劍，銜須於口，顧左右曰：「既為賊所殺，無令須汙土！

translations.literal: " Xu accepted the sword, held his beard in his mouth, looked to left and right, and said: "Since I am to be killed by bandits, do not let my beard touch the soil!
translations.idiomatic: " Xu accepted the sword, held his beard in his mouth, looked about, and said, "Since I am to be killed by bandits, do not let my beard touch the soil!"

sentences.zh: 」遂伏劍而死。

translations.literal: " He thereupon fell on the sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon fell on the sword and died.

sentences.zh: 從事王忠持其喪歸雒陽，詔賜以塚地，拜三子為郎。

translations.literal: Attendant Wang Zhong bore his coffin back to Luoyang; an edict granted burial ground and appointed his three sons as Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Zhong bore his coffin back to Luoyang; an edict granted burial ground and appointed his three sons as Gentlemen of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 5十二月，高句麗王遣使朝貢，帝復其王號。

translations.literal: 5. In the twelfth month, the king of Gaogouli sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor restored his royal title.
translations.idiomatic: 5. In the twelfth month, the king of Gaogouli sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor restored his royal title.

sentences.zh: 6是歲，大水。

translations.literal: 6. This year there was a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: 6. This year there was a great flood.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，穎陽成侯祭遵薨於軍；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, Marquis Cheng of Yingyang Ji Zun died in the army;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, Marquis Cheng of Yingyang Ji Zun died in the army;

sentences.zh: 詔馮異並將其營。

translations.literal: an edict had Feng Yi take command of his camps as well.
translations.idiomatic: an edict had Feng Yi take command of his camps as well.

sentences.zh: 遵為人，廉約小心，克己奉公，賞賜盡與士卒；

translations.literal: Zun as a man was frugal and cautious, restrained himself and served the public; rewards and gifts he gave entirely to the soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Zun was frugal and cautious, restrained himself and served the public, and gave all rewards and gifts to his soldiers;

sentences.zh: 約束嚴整，所在吏民不知有軍。

translations.literal: his discipline was strict and orderly, and wherever he was officials and people did not know an army was present.
translations.idiomatic: his discipline was strict and orderly, and wherever he was officials and commoners scarcely knew an army was present.

sentences.zh: 取士皆用儒術，對酒設樂，必雅歌投壺。

translations.literal: in recruiting scholars he used only Confucian learning; when wine was set out with music, he always had elegant songs and pitch-pot.
translations.idiomatic: in recruiting men he used only Confucian learning; when wine was set out with music, he always had elegant songs and pitch-pot.

sentences.zh: 臨終，遺戒薄葬；

translations.literal: At his end he left instructions for a plain burial;
translations.idiomatic: At his end he left instructions for a plain burial;

sentences.zh: 問以家事，終無所言。

translations.literal: asked about household affairs, he finally said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: asked about household affairs, he finally said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝愍悼之尤甚，遵喪至河南，車駕素服臨之，望哭哀慟；

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him with exceptional grief; when Zun's coffin reached Henan the imperial carriage in plain dress came to it, gazed and wept in deep sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned him with exceptional grief; when Zun's coffin reached Henan the sovereign came in plain dress, gazed upon it, and wept in deep sorrow;

sentences.zh: 還，幸城門，閱過喪車，涕泣不能已；

translations.literal: on returning he visited the city gate, reviewed the passing funeral carriage, and wept without cease;
translations.idiomatic: on returning he visited the city gate, reviewed the passing funeral carriage, and wept without cease;

sentences.zh: 喪禮成，復親祠以太牢。

translations.literal: when the funeral rites were completed he again sacrificed in person with the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: when the funeral rites were completed he again sacrificed in person with the great offering.

sentences.zh: 詔大長秋、謁者、河南尹護喪事，大司農給費。

translations.literal: An edict had the Grand Chamberlain for the Palace, the Usher, and the Intendant of Henan oversee funeral affairs; the Minister of the Imperial Granary supplied expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had the Grand Chamberlain for the Palace, the Usher, and the Intendant of Henan oversee funeral affairs; the Minister of the Imperial Granary supplied expenses.

sentences.zh: 至葬，車駕復臨之；

translations.literal: At the burial the imperial carriage again came in person;
translations.idiomatic: At the burial the sovereign again came in person;

sentences.zh: 既葬，又臨其墳，存見夫人、室家。

translations.literal: after burial he again visited the tomb and inquired after the lady and household.
translations.idiomatic: after burial he again visited the tomb and inquired after the lady and household.

sentences.zh: 其後朝會，帝每歎曰：「安得憂國奉公如祭征虜者乎！

translations.literal: Afterward at court audiences the Emperor often sighed and said: "Where can one find another who cares for the state and serves the public like Campaign-against-Barbarians Ji?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward at court audiences the Emperor often sighed and said, "Where can one find another who cares for the state and serves the public like Campaign-against-Barbarians Ji?"

sentences.zh: 」衛尉銚期曰：「陛下至仁，哀念祭遵不已，群臣各懷慚懼。

translations.literal: " Commandant of the Guards Nao Qi said: "Your Majesty is supremely humane and mourns Ji Zun without end; the ministers each harbor shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Commandant of the Guards Nao Qi said, "Your Majesty is supremely humane and mourns Ji Zun without end; the ministers each harbor shame and fear."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 2隗囂病且餓，餐糗糒，恚憤而卒。

translations.literal: 2. Wei Ao was ill and also starving; he ate dry baked grain, died in rage and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Wei Ao was ill and starving; he ate dry baked grain, and died in rage and resentment.

sentences.zh: 王元、周宗立囂少子純為王，總兵據冀。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan and Zhou Zong enthroned Ao's youngest son Chun as king, gathered troops, and held Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan and Zhou Zong enthroned Ao's youngest son Chun as king, gathered troops, and held Ji.

sentences.zh: 公孫述遣將趙匡、田弇助純。

translations.literal: Gongsun Shu sent generals Zhao Kuang and Tian Yan to assist Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu sent generals Zhao Kuang and Tian Yan to assist Chun.

sentences.zh: 帝使馮異擊之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Feng Yi to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Feng Yi to attack them.

sentences.zh: 3公孫述遣其翼江王田戎、大司徒任滿、南郡太守程泛將數萬人下江關，擊破馮駿等軍，遂拔巫及夷道、夷陵，因據荊門、虎牙，橫江水起浮橋、關樓，立欑柱以絕水道，結營跨山以塞陸路，拒漢兵。

translations.literal: 3. Gongsun Shu sent his King of Assisting Jiang Tian Rong, Grand Minister of Education Ren Man, and Administrator of Nanjun Cheng Fan to lead tens of thousands down Jiang Pass, defeated the army of Feng Jun and others, thereupon took Wu and Yidao and Yiling, and thereby held Jingmen and Huya; across the river they raised floating bridges and barrier towers, set piled pillars to cut the water route, joined camps across mountains to block the land road, and resisted Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Gongsun Shu sent his King of Assisting Jiang Tian Rong, Grand Minister of Education Ren Man, and Administrator of Nanjun Cheng Fan to lead tens of thousands down Jiang Pass, defeated Feng Jun's army, took Wu, Yidao, and Yiling, and held Jingmen and Huya; across the river they raised floating bridges and barrier towers, set piled pillars to block the water route, joined camps across the mountains to block the land road, and resisted Han troops.

sentences.zh: 4夏，六月，丙戌，帝幸緱氏，登轘轅。

translations.literal: 4. In summer, the sixth month, on bingxu, the Emperor visited Gou's clan seat and ascended Huanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In summer, the sixth month, on bingxu, the Emperor visited Gou's clan seat and ascended Huanyuan.

sentences.zh: 5吳漢率王常等四將軍兵五萬餘人擊盧芳將賈覽、閔堪於高柳；

translations.literal: 5. Wu Han led Wang Chang and three other generals with more than fifty thousand troops to attack Lu Fang's generals Jia Lan and Min Kan at Gaoliu;
translations.idiomatic: 5. Wu Han led Wang Chang and three other generals with more than fifty thousand troops to attack Lu Fang's generals Jia Lan and Min Kan at Gaoliu;

sentences.zh: 匈奴救之，漢軍不利。

translations.literal: the Xiongnu rescued them and the Han army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu rescued them and the Han army fared ill.

sentences.zh: 於是匈奴轉盛，鈔暴日增。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xiongnu grew stronger still, and raiding and violence increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Xiongnu grew stronger still, and raiding and violence increased daily.

sentences.zh: 詔朱祜屯常山，王常屯涿郡，破奸將軍侯進屯漁陽，以討虜將軍王霸為上谷太守，以備匈奴。

translations.literal: An edict had Zhu Hu encamp at Changshan, Wang Chang at Zhuo commandery, Break-Treason General Hou Jin at Yuyang, and Demon-Slaying General Wang Ba made Administrator of Shanggu to guard against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Zhu Hu encamp at Changshan, Wang Chang at Zhuo commandery, Break-Treason General Hou Jin at Yuyang, and Demon-Slaying General Wang Ba made Administrator of Shanggu to guard against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 6帝使來歙悉監護諸將屯長安，太中大夫馬援為之副。

translations.literal: 6. The Emperor sent Lai Xi to oversee in full all the generals encamped at Chang'an, with Grand Master of the Palace Ma Yuan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The Emperor sent Lai Xi to oversee in full all the generals encamped at Chang'an, with Grand Master of the Palace Ma Yuan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 歙上書曰：「公孫述以隴西、天水為籓蔽，故得延命假息；

translations.literal: Xi memorialized: "Gongsun Shu takes Longxi and Tianshui as screen and shield, and so obtains extended life and borrowed breath;
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized, "Gongsun Shu takes Longxi and Tianshui as screen and shield, and so obtains extended life and borrowed breath;

sentences.zh: 今二郡平蕩，則述智計窮矣。

translations.literal: now that the two commanderies are swept level, Shu's stratagems are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: now that the two commanderies are swept level, Shu's stratagems are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 宜益選兵馬，儲積資糧。

translations.literal: It is fitting to increase selection of troops and horses and store up provisions and grain.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to increase selection of troops and horses and store up provisions and grain.

sentences.zh: 今西州新破，兵人疲饉，若招以財穀，則其眾可集。

translations.literal: Now the Western Province is newly broken; soldiers and people are weary and hungry—if recruited with wealth and grain, their hosts can be gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Western Province is newly broken; soldiers and people are weary and hungry—if recruited with wealth and grain, their hosts can be gathered.

sentences.zh: 臣知國家所給非一，用度不足，然有不得已也！

translations.literal: Your servant knows the state's grants are not one alone and expenditures are insufficient, yet there are times when one cannot do otherwise!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant knows the state's grants are not one alone and expenditures are insufficient, yet there are times when one cannot do otherwise!"

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 於是詔於汧積穀六萬斛。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict stored grain at Qian to the amount of sixty thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict stored sixty thousand hu of grain at Qian.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，來歙率馮異等五將軍討隗純於天水。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Lai Xi led Feng Yi and four other generals to campaign against Wei Chun at Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Lai Xi led Feng Yi and four other generals to campaign against Wei Chun at Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 7驃騎將軍杜茂與賈覽戰於繁畤，茂軍敗績。

translations.literal: 7. Flying-Cavalry General Du Mao fought Jia Lan at Fanzhi; Mao's army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: 7. Flying-Cavalry General Du Mao fought Jia Lan at Fanzhi; Mao's army suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 8諸羌自王莽末入居塞內，金城屬縣多為所有。

translations.literal: 8. The various Qiang since the end of Wang Mang had entered and dwelt within the passes; many subordinate counties of Jincheng were held by them.
translations.idiomatic: 8. The various Qiang since the end of Wang Mang had entered and dwelt within the passes; many subordinate counties of Jincheng were held by them.

sentences.zh: 隗囂不能討，因就慰納，發其眾與漢相拒。

translations.literal: Wei Ao could not chastise them and thereupon went to comfort and win them, mustering their hosts to resist Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ao could not chastise them and thereupon went to comfort and win them, mustering their hosts to resist Han.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾班彪上言：「今涼州部皆有降羌，羌胡被發左衽，而與漢人雜處，習俗既異，言語不通，數為小吏黠人所見侵奪，窮恚無聊，故致反叛。

translations.literal: Chancellor's Clerk Ban Biao submitted: "Now in the Liangzhou circuit there are surrendered Qiang everywhere; Qiang and Hu with hair unbound and garments folded left live mixed with Han people; customs already differ and speech does not connect—they are repeatedly seen by petty clerks and crafty men invaded and stripped, driven to extremity with nowhere to turn, and so they come to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor's Clerk Ban Biao submitted, "Now in the Liangzhou circuit there are surrendered Qiang everywhere; Qiang and Hu with hair unbound and garments folded left live mixed with Han people; customs already differ and speech does not connect—they are repeatedly invaded and stripped by petty clerks and crafty men, driven to extremity with nowhere to turn, and so they rebel."

sentences.zh: 夫蠻夷寇亂，皆為此也。

translations.literal: Barbarian raids and disorder are all for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raids and disorder are all for this reason.

sentences.zh: 舊制，益州部置蠻夷騎都尉，幽州部置領烏桓校尉，涼州部置護羌校尉，皆持節領護，治其怨結，歲時巡行，問所疾苦。

translations.literal: The old system: in the Yizhou circuit was set the Commandant of Barbarian Cavalry; in the Youzhou circuit the Commandant in Charge of the Wuhuan; in the Liangzhou circuit the Protector of the Qiang—all bearing credentials to lead and guard, settling their grievances, and each year touring to ask their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: The old system placed in the Yizhou circuit the Commandant of Barbarian Cavalry, in the Youzhou circuit the Commandant in Charge of the Wuhuan, and in the Liangzhou circuit the Protector of the Qiang—all bearing credentials to lead and guard, settling their grievances, and each year touring to ask their hardships.

sentences.zh: 又數遣使譯，通導動靜，使塞外羌夷為吏耳目，州郡因此可得警備。

translations.literal: Again envoys and interpreters were repeatedly sent to open and guide news of movement, making Qiang and Yi beyond the passes the eyes and ears of officials, so that provinces and commanderies could thereby obtain warning and preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Again envoys and interpreters were repeatedly sent to open and guide news of movement, making Qiang and Yi beyond the passes the eyes and ears of officials, so that provinces and commanderies could thereby obtain warning and preparation.

sentences.zh: 今宜復如舊，以明威防。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to restore it as of old, to display majesty and guard against trouble.

translations.idiomatic: Niu Han was made Protector of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 9盜殺陰貴人母鄧氏及弟訢。

translations.literal: 9. Bandits killed the Honored Lady of Yin Yin Deng and her brother Xin.
translations.idiomatic: 9. Bandits killed the Honored Lady of Yin Yin Deng and her brother Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝其傷之，封貴人弟就為宣恩侯，復召就兄侍中興，欲封之，置印綬於前。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply grieved; he enfeoffed the Honored Lady's younger brother Jiu as Marquis of Proclaiming Grace, again summoned Jiu's elder brother, Palace Attendant Xing, wished to enfeoff him, and set seal and cord before him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply grieved; he enfeoffed the Honored Lady's younger brother Jiu as Marquis of Proclaiming Grace, again summoned Jiu's elder brother, Palace Attendant Xing, wished to enfeoff him, and set seal and cord before him.

sentences.zh: 興固讓曰：「臣未有先登陷陣之功，而一家數人，並蒙爵士，令天下觖望，誠所不願！

translations.literal: Xing firmly declined: "Your servant has no merit of being first to ascend and break the battle line, yet several in one family all receive noble rank—this makes the realm resentful; it is truly what I do not wish!
translations.idiomatic: Xing firmly declined, "Your servant has no merit of being first to ascend and break the battle line, yet several in one family all receive noble rank—this makes the realm resentful; it is truly what I do not wish!"

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉之，不奪其志。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised him and did not override his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor praised him and did not override his intent.

sentences.zh: 貴人問其故，興曰：「夫外戚家苦不知謙退，嫁女欲配侯王，取婦眄睨公主，愚心實不安也。

translations.literal: The Honored Lady asked the reason; Xing said: "The trouble with affinal kin is not knowing humility and withdrawal—marrying a daughter they wish to match with marquises and kings, taking a wife they cast sidelong glances at princesses; this foolish heart is truly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Lady asked the reason; Xing said, "The trouble with affinal kin is not knowing humility and withdrawal—marrying a daughter they wish to match with marquises and kings, taking a wife they cast sidelong glances at princesses; this foolish heart is truly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 富貴有極，人當知足，誇奢益為觀聽所譏。

translations.literal: Wealth and honor have their limit; a man ought to know sufficiency—boasting extravagance is further what observers ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and honor have their limit; a man ought to know sufficiency—boasting extravagance is further what observers ridicule.

sentences.zh: 」貴人感其言，深自降挹，卒不為宗親求位。

translations.literal: " The Honored Lady was moved by his words, deeply lowered and restrained herself, and finally did not seek offices for her kin.
translations.idiomatic: " The Honored Lady was moved by his words, deeply lowered and restrained herself, and finally did not seek offices for her kin.

sentences.zh: 10帝召寇恂還，以漁陽太守郭人及為潁川太守。

translations.literal: 10. The Emperor summoned Kou Xun back and made Yuyang Administrator Guo Renji Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: 10. The Emperor summoned Kou Xun back and made Yuyang Administrator Guo Renji Administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 人及招降山賊趙宏、召吳等數百人，皆遣歸附農；

translations.literal: Renji summoned and received the surrender of mountain bandits Zhao Hong, Shao Wu, and several hundred others, all sent back to attach to farming;
translations.idiomatic: Renji summoned and received the surrender of mountain bandits Zhao Hong, Shao Wu, and several hundred others, all sent back to attach to farming;

sentences.zh: 因自劾專命，帝不以咎之。

translations.literal: he thereupon impeached himself for acting on his own authority; the Emperor did not blame him for it.
translations.idiomatic: he thereupon impeached himself for acting on his own authority; the Emperor did not blame him for it.

sentences.zh: 後宏、吳等黨與聞人及威信，遠自江南，或從幽、冀，不期俱降，駱驛不絕。

translations.literal: Later Hong, Wu, and their associates, hearing of Renji's prestige and trust, came from afar—from Jiangnan, or from You and Ji—unexpectedly all submitting together, post relays without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hong, Wu, and their associates, hearing of Renji's prestige and trust, came from afar—from Jiangnan, or from You and Ji—unexpectedly all submitting together, post relays without cease.

sentences.zh: 11莎車王康卒，弟賢立，攻殺拘彌、西夜王，而使康兩子王之。

translations.literal: 11. King Kang of Suoche died; his younger brother Xian succeeded, attacked and killed the kings of Jumi and Xiye, and set Kang's two sons to rule them.
translations.idiomatic: 11. King Kang of Suoche died; his younger brother Xian succeeded, attacked and killed the kings of Jumi and Xiye, and set Kang's two sons to rule them.

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, Wu Han again led Captive-Slayer General Wang Ba and three other generals with sixty thousand men out from Gaoliu to attack Jia Lan; several thousand Xiongnu horsemen rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, Wu Han again led Captive-Slayer General Wang Ba and three other generals with sixty thousand men out from Gaoliu to attack Jia Lan; several thousand Xiongnu horsemen rescued him.

sentences.zh: 連戰於平城下，破走之。

translations.literal: They joined battle repeatedly below Pingcheng and routed and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: They joined battle repeatedly below Pingcheng and routed and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 2夏陽節侯馮異等與趙匡、田弇戰且一年，皆斬之。

translations.literal: 2. Marquis Jie of Xiayang Feng Yi and others fought Zhao Kuang and Tian Yan for nearly a year and beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Marquis Jie of Xiayang Feng Yi and others fought Zhao Kuang and Tian Yan for nearly a year and beheaded them both.

translations.literal: Wei Chun was not yet taken; the generals wished to withdraw for the time being and rest the troops; Yi firmly held and did not move, and together they attacked Luomen but did not take it.

translations.literal: this is one place of ease from which the four quarters may be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: this is one place of ease from which the four quarters may be controlled.

sentences.zh: 今士馬疲倦，方履險阻，非萬乘之固也。

translations.literal: Now soldiers and horses are weary and you are just treading perilous passes—it is not the security of the imperial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Now soldiers and horses are weary and you are just treading perilous passes—it is not the security of the imperial chariot.

sentences.zh: 前年潁川，可為至戒。

translations.literal: The affair at Yingchuan two years ago may serve as the utmost warning.
translations.idiomatic: The affair at Yingchuan two years ago may serve as the utmost warning.

translations.idiomatic: Jun still did not submit; the Emperor sent Kou Xun to go and receive his surrender.

sentences.zh: 恂奉璽書至第一，峻遣軍師皇甫文出謁，辭禮不屈；

translations.literal: Xun bore the imperial letter on jade to the First; Jun sent his Military Adviser Huangfu Wen out to call on him, but in words and ceremony he would not yield;
translations.idiomatic: Xun bore the imperial letter on jade to the First; Jun sent his Military Adviser Huangfu Wen out to call on him, but in words and ceremony he would not yield;

sentences.zh: 恂怒，將誅之。

translations.literal: Xun was angered and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was angered and was about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 諸將諫曰：「高峻精兵萬人，率多強弩，西遮隴道，連年不下，今欲降之而反戮其使，無乃不可乎？

translations.literal: The generals remonstrated: "Gao Jun has elite troops of ten thousand, mostly strong crossbows; he blocks the Long road in the west and for successive years has not been taken—now you wish to receive his surrender yet instead kill his envoy—is this not inadmissible?
translations.idiomatic: The generals remonstrated, "Gao Jun has elite troops of ten thousand, mostly strong crossbows; he blocks the Long road in the west and for successive years has not been taken—now you wish to receive his surrender yet instead kill his envoy—is this not inadmissible?"

sentences.zh: 」恂不應，遂斬之，遣其副歸告峻曰：「軍師無禮，已戮之矣！

translations.literal: " Xun did not reply, thereupon beheaded him, and sent his deputy back to tell Jun: "The Military Adviser was without courtesy—I have already executed him!
translations.idiomatic: " Xun did not reply, thereupon beheaded him, and sent his deputy back to tell Jun, "The Military Adviser was without courtesy—I have already executed him!"

sentences.zh: 欲降，急降；

translations.literal: If you wish to submit, submit quickly;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to submit, submit quickly;

sentences.zh: 不欲，固守！

translations.literal: if not, hold firm!
translations.idiomatic: if not, hold firm!

sentences.zh: 」峻惶恐，即日開城門降。

translations.literal: " Jun was terrified and that very day opened the city gate and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was terrified and that very day opened the city gate and submitted.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆賀，因曰：「敢問殺其使而降其城，何也？

translations.literal: The generals all congratulated him and thereupon said: "We venture to ask—killing his envoy yet receiving the surrender of his city—how is this?
translations.idiomatic: The generals all congratulated him and thereupon said, "We venture to ask—killing his envoy yet receiving the surrender of his city—how is this?"

sentences.zh: 」恂曰：「皇甫文，峻之腹心，其所取計者也。

translations.literal: " Kou Xun said: "Huangfu Wen is Jun's trusted inner man—the one from whom he takes his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Xun said, "Huangfu Wen is Gao Jun's trusted inner counselor—the one from whom he takes his plans.

sentences.zh: 今來，辭意不屈，必無降心。

translations.literal: Now he has come with language and intent unyielding; he surely has no heart to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Now he has come with language and intent unyielding; he surely has no heart to surrender.

sentences.zh: 全之則文得其計，殺之則峻亡其膽，是以降耳。

translations.literal: If we spare him, Wen gets his plan across; if we kill him, Jun loses his courage—that is why he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: If we spare him, Wen gets his plan across; if we kill him, Gao Jun loses his courage—that is why he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「非所及也！

translations.literal: " The generals all said: "Beyond what we could reach!
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Beyond what we could reach!"

sentences.zh: 5冬，十月，來歙與諸將攻破落門，周宗、行巡、苟宇、趙恢等將隗純降，王元奔蜀。

translations.literal: 5 Winter, tenth month, Lai Xi with the generals broke Luomen; Zhou Zong, Xing Xun, Gou Yu, Zhao Hui, and others led Wei Chun to surrender; Wang Yuan fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, in winter, in the tenth month, Lai Xi and the generals broke Luomen; Zhou Zong, Xing Xun, Gou Yu, Zhao Hui, and others led Wei Chun to surrender; Wang Yuan fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 徙諸隗於京師以東。

translations.literal: The various Wei clansmen were moved east of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The various Wei clansmen were relocated east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 後隗純與賓客亡入胡，至武威，捕得，誅之。

translations.literal: Later Wei Chun with his guests fled into the Hu lands; reaching Wuwei they were captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Chun fled into the barbarian lands with his guests; reaching Wuwei they were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 6先零羌與諸種寇金城、隴西，來歙率蓋延等進擊，大破之，斬首虜數千人。

translations.literal: 6 The Xianling Qiang with various tribes raided Jincheng and Longxi; Lai Xi led Gai Yan and others forward to strike, routed them greatly, and beheaded and captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Xianling Qiang and various tribes raided Jincheng and Longxi; Lai Xi led Gai Yan and others in attack, routed them completely, and beheaded and captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 於是開倉稟以賑饑乏，隴右遂安，而涼州流通焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they opened granaries and distributed grain to relieve hunger and want; Longyou was thereby pacified, and Liangzhou commerce flowed again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they opened granaries and distributed grain to relieve hunger and want; Longyou was thereby pacified, and commerce in Liangzhou flowed again.

translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others seized the momentum and fought to the death; they hurled fire torches to burn it; wind fed the flames until they were fierce and the bridge towers collapsed in fire.

sentences.zh: 岑彭悉軍順風並進，所向無前，蜀兵大亂，溺死者數千人，斬任滿，生獲程汎，而田戎走保江州。

translations.literal: Cen Peng led the whole army with the wind in parallel advance, unstoppable wherever they went; Shu troops fell into great disorder; several thousand drowned; Ren Man was beheaded, Cheng Fan captured alive, and Tian Rong fled to hold Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Peng led the whole army with the wind in parallel advance, unstoppable wherever they went; Shu troops fell into great disorder; several thousand drowned; Ren Man was beheaded, Cheng Fan was captured alive, and Tian Rong fled to hold Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彭上劉隆為南郡太守；

translations.literal: Peng recommended Liu Long as Administrator of Nan commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Peng recommended Liu Long as Administrator of Nan commandery;

sentences.zh: 自率輔威將軍臧宮、驍騎將軍劉歆長驅入江關。

translations.literal: himself led Auxiliary Majestic General Zang Gong and Valiant Cavalry General Liu Xin in a long drive into the Jiang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: himself led Auxiliary Majestic General Zang Gong and Valiant Cavalry General Liu Xin in a long drive into the Jiang Pass.

sentences.zh: 令軍中無得虜掠，所過，百姓皆奉牛酒迎勞，彭復讓不受。

translations.literal: He ordered that within the army there was to be no seizing plunder; wherever they passed the common people all offered oxen and wine to welcome and refresh them—Peng again declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that within the army there was to be no seizing plunder; wherever they passed the common people all offered oxen and wine to welcome and refresh them, but Peng again declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 百姓大喜，爭開門降。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased and vied to open their gates and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were greatly pleased and vied to open their gates and surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔彭守益州牧，所下郡輒行太守事，彭若出界，即以太守號付後將軍。

translations.literal: An edict made Peng acting Governor of Yizhou; in each commandery he reached he at once exercised the Administrator's duties; if Peng crossed the border, the title of Administrator was handed to the Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Peng acting Governor of Yizhou; in each commandery he reached he at once exercised the Administrator's duties; if Peng crossed the border, the title of Administrator was handed to the Rear General.

sentences.zh: 選官屬守州中長吏。

translations.literal: He selected officials and staff to hold the long-term offices within the province.
translations.idiomatic: He selected officials and staff to hold the long-term offices within the province.

sentences.zh: 彭到江州，以其城固糧多，難卒拔，留馮駿守之；

translations.literal: Peng reached Jiangzhou; because its walls were strong and grain abundant and it could not quickly be taken, he left Feng Jun to hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Peng reached Jiangzhou; because its walls were strong and grain abundant and it could not quickly be taken, he left Feng Jun to hold it;

sentences.zh: 自引兵乘利直指墊江，攻破平曲，收其米數十萬石。

translations.literal: himself led troops, seizing advantage, straight at Dianjiang, broke Pingqu, and gathered several hundred thousand shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: himself led troops, seizing advantage, straight at Dianjiang, broke Pingqu, and gathered several hundred thousand shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 吳漢留夷陵，裝露橈繼進。

translations.literal: Wu Han remained at Yiling, fitting out uncovered oars and continuing forward.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han remained at Yiling, fitting out uncovered oars and continuing forward.

sentences.zh: 3夏，先零羌寇臨洮。

translations.literal: 3 Summer, the Xianling Qiang raided Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, in summer, the Xianling Qiang raided Lintao.

sentences.zh: 來歙薦馬援為隴西太守，擊先零羌，大破之。

translations.literal: Lai Xi recommended Ma Yuan as Administrator of Longxi; he struck the Xianling Qiang and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Xi recommended Ma Yuan as Administrator of Longxi; he struck the Xianling Qiang and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 4公孫述以王元為將軍，使與領軍環安拒河池。

translations.literal: 4 Gongsun Shu made Wang Yuan a general and sent him with Colonel of the Guard Huan An to hold Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Gongsun Shu made Wang Yuan a general and sent him with Colonel of the Guard Huan An to hold Hechi.

sentences.zh: 六月，來歙與蓋延等進攻元、安，大破之，遂克下辨，乘勝遂進。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Lai Xi with Gai Yan and others advanced to attack Yuan and An, routed them greatly, then took Xiabian and pressed the victory forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Lai Xi with Gai Yan and others advanced to attack Yuan and An, routed them completely, then took Xiabian and pressed the victory forward.

sentences.zh: 蜀人大懼，使刺客刺歙，未殊，馳召蓋延。

translations.literal: Shu people were greatly afraid and sent assassins to stab Xi; he was not yet dead and urgently summoned Gai Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were greatly afraid and sent assassins to stab Lai Xi; he was not yet dead and urgently summoned Gai Yan.

sentences.zh: 延見歙，因伏悲哀，不能仰視。

translations.literal: Yan saw Xi and thereupon prostrated himself in grief, unable to look up.
translations.idiomatic: Yan saw Xi and thereupon prostrated himself in grief, unable to look up.

sentences.zh: 歙叱延曰：「虎牙何敢然！

translations.literal: Xi rebuked Yan: "Tiger's Tooth, how dare you act thus!
translations.idiomatic: Xi rebuked Yan, "Tiger's Tooth, how dare you act thus!

sentences.zh: 今使者中刺客，無以報國，故呼巨卿，欲相屬以軍事，而反效兒女子涕泣乎！

translations.literal: Now the envoy has been struck by assassins and cannot repay the state—therefore I called Great Qing, wishing to entrust you with military affairs, yet you instead imitate children and women in weeping!
translations.idiomatic: Now the envoy has been struck by assassins and cannot repay the state—therefore I called you, Great Qing, wishing to entrust you with military affairs, yet you instead imitate children and women in weeping!

sentences.zh: 刃雖在身，不能勒兵斬公邪？

translations.literal: Though the blade is in my body, can you not muster troops and behead the lord?
translations.idiomatic: Though the blade is in my body, can you not muster troops and behead the enemy lord?"

sentences.zh: 」延收淚強起，受所誡。

translations.literal: " Yan wiped his tears, forced himself to rise, and received the charge given him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wiped his tears, forced himself to rise, and received the charge given him.

sentences.zh: 歙自書表曰：「臣夜人定後，為何人所賊傷，中臣要害。

translations.literal: Xi himself wrote a memorial saying: "Your servant, after men had settled at night, was wounded by assassins—struck in my vital place.
translations.idiomatic: Xi himself wrote a memorial, saying, "Your servant, after men had settled at night, was wounded by assassins—struck in my vital place.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢自惜，誠恨奉職不稱，以為朝廷羞。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not spare himself but truly regrets that in fulfilling duty I have not measured up, bringing shame on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dares not spare himself but truly regrets that in fulfilling duty I have not measured up, bringing shame on the court.

sentences.zh: 夫理國以得賢為本，太中大夫段襄，骨鯁可任，願陛下裁察。

translations.literal: To order a state, gaining the worthy is fundamental; Grand Master of the Palace Duan Xiang is a backbone who can be entrusted—may Your Majesty judge and examine.
translations.idiomatic: To order a state, gaining the worthy is fundamental; Grand Master of the Palace Duan Xiang is a backbone who can be entrusted—may Your Majesty judge and examine.

sentences.zh: 又臣兄弟不肖，終恐被罪，陛下哀憐，數賜教督。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant's brothers are unworthy and in the end will surely incur guilt—may Your Majesty pity and repeatedly grant instruction and oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover your servant's brothers are unworthy and in the end will surely incur guilt—may Your Majesty pity them and repeatedly grant instruction and oversight.

sentences.zh: 」投筆抽刃而絕。

translations.literal: " He cast down the brush, drew out the blade, and expired.
translations.idiomatic: He cast down the brush, drew out the blade, and expired.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，大驚，省書攬涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard, was greatly startled, read the memorial, and clasped it while weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard, was greatly startled, read the memorial, and wept as he clasped it.

sentences.zh: 以揚武將軍馬成守中郎將代之。

translations.literal: He made Valiant Martial General Ma Cheng hold the post of Colonel of the Palace Guard in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He made Valiant Martial General Ma Cheng hold the post of Colonel of the Palace Guard in his stead.

sentences.zh: 歙喪還洛陽，乘輿縞素臨吊、送葬。

translations.literal: When Xi's funeral returned to Luoyang, the imperial carriage in unbleached silk came to mourn and escort the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi's funeral returned to Luoyang, the Emperor in unbleached silk came to mourn and escort the burial.

sentences.zh: 5趙王良從帝送歙喪還，入夏城門，與中郎將張邯爭道，叱邯旋車，又詰責門候，使前走數十步。

translations.literal: 5 King Zhao Liang followed the Emperor escorting Xi's funeral back; entering the Xia city gate he disputed the road with Colonel of the Palace Guard Zhang Han, rebuked Han to turn his carriage, and also reproached the gate warden, making him go forward several tens of paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year King Zhao Liang followed the Emperor escorting Xi's funeral back; entering the Xia city gate he disputed the road with Colonel of the Palace Guard Zhang Han, rebuked Han to turn his carriage, and also reproached the gate warden, making him go forward several tens of paces.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉鮑永劾奏：「良無籓臣禮，大不敬。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Bao Yong impeached him: "Liang lacks the rites of a feudatory minister—great irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Bao Yong impeached him, saying, "Liang lacks the rites of a feudatory minister—great irreverence."

sentences.zh: 」良尊戚貴重，而永劾之，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: " Liang was a honored kinsman of weighty rank, yet Yong impeached him—the court was awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was an honored kinsman of weighty rank, yet Bao Yong impeached him—the court was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 永辟扶風鮑恢為都官從事，恢亦抗直，不避強禦。

translations.literal: Yong recruited Bao Hui of Fufeng as Director of Capital Cases; Hui was also upright and unyielding, not avoiding the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yong recruited Bao Hui of Fufeng as Director of Capital Cases; Hui was also upright and unyielding and did not avoid the powerful.

sentences.zh: 帝常曰：「貴戚且斂手以避二鮑。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said: "Even the honored kin fold their hands to avoid the two Baos.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often said, "Even the honored kin fold their hands to avoid the two Baos."

sentences.zh: 」永行縣到霸陵，路經更始墓，下拜，哭盡哀而去，西至扶風，椎牛上苟諫塚。

translations.literal: " Yong on circuit reached Baling; the road passed Gengshi's tomb—he dismounted, bowed, wept his full grief, and departed; west to Fufeng he beat an ox as offering atop Gou Jian's mound.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yong on circuit reached Baling; the road passed Gengshi's tomb—he dismounted, bowed, wept his full grief, and departed; west to Fufeng he beat an ox as offering atop Gou Jian's mound.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，意不平，問公卿曰：「奉使如此，何如？

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and was ill at ease; he asked the high ministers: "To go on commission like this—how is it?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and was ill at ease; he asked the high ministers, "To go on commission like this—how is it?"

sentences.zh: 」太中大夫張湛對曰：「仁者，行之宗；

translations.literal: " Grand Master of the Palace Zhang Zhan replied: "Benevolence is the ancestor of conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Palace Zhang Zhan replied, "Benevolence is the ancestor of conduct;

sentences.zh: 忠者，義之主也。

translations.literal: loyalty is the master of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty is the master of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 仁不遺舊，忠不忘君，行之高者也。

translations.literal: Benevolence does not abandon the old; loyalty does not forget the lord—these are the heights of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence does not abandon the old; loyalty does not forget the lord—these are the heights of conduct."

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃釋。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mind was then released.

sentences.zh: 6帝自將征公孫述；

translations.literal: 6 The Emperor himself led the campaign against Gongsun Shu;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Emperor himself led the campaign against Gongsun Shu;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，次長安。

translations.literal: autumn, seventh month, he halted at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, in the seventh month, he halted at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 7公孫述使其將延岑、呂鮪、王元、公孫恢悉兵拒廣漢及資中，又遣將侯丹率二萬餘人拒黃石。

translations.literal: 7 Gongsun Shu sent his generals Yan Cen, Lü Fu, Wang Yuan, and Gongsun Hui with all their troops to hold Guanghan and Zizhong, and also sent General Hou Dan leading more than twenty thousand men to hold Huangshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Gongsun Shu sent his generals Yan Cen, Lü Fu, Wang Yuan, and Gongsun Hui with all their troops to hold Guanghan and Zizhong, and also sent General Hou Dan with more than twenty thousand men to hold Huangshi.

sentences.zh: 岑彭使臧宮將降卒五萬，從涪水上平曲，拒延岑，自分兵浮江下還江州，溯都江而上，襲擊侯丹，大破之；

translations.literal: Cen Peng sent Zang Gong leading fifty thousand surrendered troops up the Fu River from Pingshui to Pingqu to hold Yan Cen; he himself divided troops to float down the river back to Jiangzhou, go up the Du River, and strike Hou Dan, routing him greatly;
translations.idiomatic: Cen Peng sent Zang Gong with fifty thousand surrendered troops up the Fu River from Pingshui to Pingqu to hold Yan Cen; he himself divided troops to float down the river back to Jiangzhou, go up the Du River, and strike Hou Dan, routing him completely;

sentences.zh: 因晨夜倍道兼行二千餘里，逕拔武陽。

translations.literal: then day and night on double marches traveled more than two thousand li and straightway took Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: then traveled more than two thousand li day and night on forced marches and straightway took Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 使精騎馳擊廣都，去成都數十里，勢若風雨，所至皆奔散。

translations.literal: He sent elite cavalry to gallop and strike Guangdu, several tens of li from Chengdu; their momentum was like wind and rain—wherever they reached all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent elite cavalry to gallop and strike Guangdu, several tens of li from Chengdu; their momentum was like wind and rain—wherever they reached all fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 初，述聞漢兵在平曲，故遣大兵逆之。

translations.literal: At first Shu heard Han troops were at Pingqu and therefore sent a great army to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gongsun Shu heard Han troops were at Pingqu and therefore sent a great army to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 及彭至武陽，繞出延岑軍後，蜀地震駭。

translations.literal: When Peng reached Wuyang and came out behind Yan Cen's army, Shu was shaken as by an earthquake in terror.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng reached Wuyang and came out behind Yan Cen's army, Shu was shaken as by an earthquake in terror.

sentences.zh: 述大驚，以杖擊地曰：「是何神也！

translations.literal: Shu was greatly startled, struck the ground with his staff, and said: "What god is this!
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu was greatly startled, struck the ground with his staff, and said, "What god is this!"
